12	
13	# Task sizing — the 5-axis routing rubric
14	
15	This rubric routes a single task to a **model tier** and a **review-attention flag** at planning time. It is risk-weighted *routing*, not effort estimation: the output is "which model should run this, and how much review does it warrant," never "how long will this take." You score five axes Low/Med/High, the stakes axis sets a default direction, the other axes adjust it, and a tier and a flag fall out.
16	
17	Routing is not cascading. **Routing** is planning-time pre-classification — one model is chosen per task *before* it runs. **Cascading** is runtime escalation — start on a cheap model and retry on a bigger one mid-execution when the cheap one fails. This rubric only does routing; cascading is a named, separate, out-of-scope layer (see *What this is not for*).
18	
19	**Reconciliation with eng-agentic P8.** P8 says effort is measured in slices and gates, not calendar time, and warns against importing a "how long will this take" frame. A sizing rubric could look like it smuggles effort estimation back in. It does not: it emits a capability tier keyed to *risk*, never a duration or a size. It is orthogonal to — and applied *after* — the slice-based Size check performed during at-pickup task breakdown. Two lenses on the same already-sized slice: one asks "is this one verifiable change" (Size), the other asks "what does it cost to get it wrong, and what capability does it need" (this rubric). Neither uses calendar time.
20	
21	## The 5 active axes
22	
23	Score each axis Low / Med / High by **routing pressure** — High means "argues for a more capable model." Four axes read naturally (more demanding = higher pressure). **Specification completeness runs inverted**: a *less* complete spec is *higher* pressure, because the model must infer intent rather than follow it.
24	
25	| Axis | Low pressure | Medium | High pressure |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| **Reasoning complexity** | mechanical edit, lookup, rename, reformat | bounded logic following a known pattern | open-ended design, cross-cutting synthesis, subtle algorithmic correctness |
28	| **Specification completeness** *(inverted)* | fully specified — concrete acceptance criteria, named files, no judgment left | mostly specified, a few gaps to fill | sparse or ambiguous — intent must be inferred, acceptance criteria absent |
29	| **Hallucination sensitivity** | self-contained; no external API or library surface | familiar, stable APIs the model knows well | unfamiliar or fast-moving APIs, version-specific behaviour, high fabricated-signature risk |
30	| **Stakes / reversibility** | trivially reversible two-way door — one file, easy revert, low blast radius | reversible with effort; bounded blast radius | one-way door — schema migration, public API, auth, production data, security |
31	| **Orchestration role** | leaf worker on a single delegated slice | worker doing local sequencing within its slice | orchestrator — decomposes, delegates, integrates sub-agent output |
32	
33	## Set-aside dimensions
34	
35	Three dimensions that matter for production routing are **near-constant for slice-bounded async dev tasks**, so they do not discriminate between tasks here and are deliberately not scored:
36	
37	- **Cost / volume** — a planning-time slice runs once, not at scale. Per-task cost is dominated by the tier you pick, not by call volume, so volume is ~1 across every task and tells you nothing.
38	- **Latency** — no human waits in real time on an async slice; seconds-vs-minutes never trades off against output quality, so wall-clock latency does not move the routing.
39	- **Context size** — slices are already size-checked to one verifiable change (Step 5), so the working set fits comfortably inside every tier's context window; context length rarely forces a tier.
40	
41	If a task violates one of these assumptions (a real-time path, a high-QPS call site, a genuinely large working set), it is not a slice-bounded async dev task and this rubric is the wrong tool.
42	
43	## Model tiers
44	
45	**`Fast = Haiku 4.5` · `Balanced = Sonnet 4.6` · `Frontier = Opus 4.7`.** (One mapping line by design: a model bump is a one-line edit here, not a rewrite of every reference to a tier.)
46	
47	**Orchestrator / worker.** The default assignment is static, not per-call: an orchestrator (decomposes, delegates, integrates) runs **Frontier**; workers run **Balanced**; mechanical leaf workers drop to **Fast**. This is the orchestrator/worker pattern, applied at planning time — not runtime model selection.
48	
49	## Routing rule (reversibility-gated)
50	
51	Stakes/reversibility sets the default direction; the capability axes adjust it. Grounded in eng-universal P3 — deliberation scales with cost-of-reversal, not with how hard the task feels.
52	
53	1. **Set the floor from stakes/reversibility.**
54	   - One-way door / high-stakes (**SR = High**) → **default up**: floor is **Frontier**. The cost of being wrong dominates the cost of the model; any downgrade needs a written reason.
55	   - Reversible / mechanical (**SR = Low/Med**) → **default down**: floor is **Fast**. Escalate only on a *demonstrated* capability gap, not on suspicion.
56	2. **Lift for capability.** Among the three capability axes — reasoning complexity, specification completeness, hallucination sensitivity — each one at **High pressure** lifts the tier one step above the floor (Fast → Balanced → Frontier), capped at Frontier. (This is the "escalate on a capability gap" path for reversible tasks.)
57	3. **Orchestrator pin.** Orchestration role **High** pins **Frontier** outright — the orchestrator's mistakes propagate to every worker it directs.
58	4. **Resolve the SR = Med middle upward.** SR = Med shares the Fast floor with Low, but its blast radius is real, not trivial. When a capability axis is borderline (you could defensibly call it Med or High) on an SR = Med task, score it High and take the lift — this is the bounded-but-real case P3 says to deliberate over.
59	
60	## Derived outputs
61	
62	The score produces three things — review load is an *output* of the axes, never an input:
63	
64	1. **Model tier** — Fast / Balanced / Frontier, from the routing rule above.
65	2. **Review-attention flag** — `elevated` when **SR = High** *or* **HS = High**; otherwise `standard`. This tells review where to spend the asymmetric second-pass attention (eng-agentic Part 2: review matters more under agents).
66	3. **Companion-skill triggers** — fired by a single High axis:
67	   - **HS = High** → run `source-driven-development` on the task: verify every API and signature against current docs before relying on it (eng-agentic P2 — hallucination is the default, sources are the brake).
68	   - **SR = High** → run a `code-review-and-quality` pass before merge (escalate to `security-and-hardening` when the one-way door is auth, secrets, or a destructive/PII data operation — a schema migration or backfill is the ordinary `code-review-and-quality` case).
69	
70	## Annotation one-liner format
71	
72	Every task in a filed task list carries one routing line. It **must begin with `Model:`** (the conformance check is `grep -L 'Model:' docs/tasks/*.md` returning nothing). The axis vector is positional and fixed-order so two independent applications diff cleanly: `RC · SC · HS · SR · OR`.
73	
74	```
75	Model: <Fast|Balanced|Frontier> · risk <reversible|one-way> · review <standard|elevated> · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = <L|M|H>·<L|M|H>·<L|M|H>·<L|M|H>·<L|M|H>[ · companions <skill[, skill]>]
76	```
77	
78	The `companions` segment is omitted when no companion trigger fires.
79	
80	## Worked example
81	
82	**Task:** "Write a function that deduplicates overlapping calendar events, merging adjacent ones."
83	
84	| Axis | Score | Rationale |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| Reasoning complexity | **High** | interval-merge logic with non-obvious edge cases (touching vs overlapping, zero-length) — subtle algorithmic correctness |
87	| Specification completeness | Med | behaviour described; the adjacency rule and tie-handling need inference |
88	| Hallucination sensitivity | Low | pure logic, no external API surface |
89	| Stakes / reversibility | Low | one pure function, covered by unit tests, trivially reverted — two-way door |
90	| Orchestration role | Low | leaf worker |
91	
92	**Derivation.** SR = Low → floor **Fast**. One capability axis at High (reasoning complexity) lifts one step → **Balanced**. No orchestrator pin. Review flag: SR and HS both not High → `standard`. No companion trigger.
93	
94	```
95	Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L
96	```
97	
98	**Contrast — same rubric, different tiers** (shows the gate discriminates):
99	
100	| Task | RC·SC·HS·SR·OR | Tier | Review | Why |
101	|---|---|---|---|---|
102	| Rename a column reference across the codebase | L·L·L·L·L | **Fast** | standard | all low pressure; mechanical, reversible |
103	| Add a migration renaming `users.email` and backfilling it | M·M·M·H·L | **Frontier** | elevated | SR = High one-way door sets the Frontier floor; `companions code-review-and-quality` |
104	
105	## Common miscalibrations
106	
107	**Scoring spec completeness like the others.** It is inverted. A fully-specified task is *Low* pressure; marking "well-specified = High" routes trivial tasks to Frontier. Read the column header, not the word.
108	
109	**Routing on effort instead of risk.** "This is a big task, give it Opus." Size is verification granularity — a big task is split into slices (Step 5), and each slice is routed on its own axes. Effort is never an input here.
110	
111	**Escalating on suspicion.** For reversible tasks the default is down. "Might be tricky" is not a demonstrated capability gap. Start at the floor; escalate when the cheaper tier actually fails the task, not when it might.
112	
113	**Letting stakes touch only the review flag.** A one-way door sets *both* the tier floor (Frontier) and the review flag (elevated). Routing a risky task to Fast "because review will catch it" inverts the rule — the model that opens the door should be the capable one.
114	
115	**Scoring an orchestrator as a worker.** If the task decomposes and delegates, orchestration role is High → Frontier, however simple any single sub-task looks. The orchestrator's errors propagate to every worker downstream.
116	
117	## What this is not for
118	
119	- **Not effort or time estimation.** The output is a tier and a flag — never hours, days, or story points (eng-agentic P8). Reaching for "this'll take a while" means you are in the wrong rubric.
120	- **Not a runtime cascade.** This is planning-time routing: one model chosen per task before it runs. Mid-execution escalation to a bigger model is a separate, named, out-of-scope layer.
121	- **Not a replacement for the verification-granularity Size check.** The at-pickup task breakdown phase sizes each task by whether it is one verifiable slice. This rubric is a second lens applied *after* that check passes — it routes the already-sized slice. A task that is too big is split first, then each slice is routed.
122	
123	## Sources
124	
125	- Anthropic — "Models overview" and "Choosing the right model" (capabilities / speed / cost triad; tier selection)
126	- Anthropic — "Building a multi-agent research system" (orchestrator/worker pattern)
127	- Augment — "AI model routing guide"; TianPan — "LLM routing vs model cascades" (routing vs cascading distinction)
128	- `rules/eng-principles-universal.md` — P3 (architecture is the expensive-to-change decisions; one-way vs two-way doors; reversibility-gated deliberation)
129	- `rules/eng-principles-agentic.md` — P2 (hallucination is the default, sources are the brake), P8 (effort is measured in slices and gates, not calendar time)
130	- `skills/delivery-shape/SKILL.md` — at-pickup task breakdown (verification granularity), the discipline this rubric routes to
131

1	# Delivery plan — Top-down delivery planning
2	
3	A worked delivery plan for one real, already-shaped initiative, **produced by hand** in the
4	walking-skeleton spike. It is the evidence half of the `delivery-shape` contract: the schema in
5	[`docs/delivery-shape-contract.md`](../../../docs/delivery-shape-contract.md) was read off *this*
6	file-set. (The spike that produced it — N01 — is itself a node in the plan; the plan is
7	self-describing.)
8	
9	**Source initiative:** [Top-down delivery planning — framing baked in, foundational work never
10	silent](https://linear.app/ababushkin/project/top-down-delivery-planning-framing-baked-in-foundational-work-never-352e1fe0c3b8)
11	· Linear `ABA` · Type 1 (methodology skill pack). Source one-pager:
12	[`docs/ideas/delivery-shape.md`](../../../docs/ideas/delivery-shape.md).
13	
14	---
15	
16	## The bet (read this first — top-down starts at the outcome)
17	
18	**Goal:** For Anton and any agent invoking Shaper, make a committed initiative produce its full
19	delivery plan top-down — deliverables → nodes (stories, capabilities, spikes, …) → verifiable
20	tasks — with framing baked in and foundational work never silently dropped.
21	
22	| KR | Claim | Role | Served by |
23	|----|-------|------|-----------|
24	| **KR1** *(commit)* | A documented plan-artefact contract + a worked file-set exist, and a walk-script converts the file-set into the expected tracker manifest. | foundation | **D1** |
25	| **KR2** *(stretch)* | On a self-trial against 2 already-shaped initiatives, the emitted plan carries AC on every story and ≥1 explicit foundational/walking-skeleton task, at 0 framing re-prompts. | bet | **D2** |
26	| **KR3** *(commit)* | On a fixed eval set of 8–10 "plan a project" phrasings, delivery-shape is the selected skill, with 0 collisions against initiative-shape or execution-breakdown. | brake | **D3** |
27	
28	**Appetite:** ~9 issues (= 9 nodes below). **Kill condition:** if the walking-skeleton spike (KR1)
29	can't produce a markdown file-set that walks deterministically and converts mechanically — i.e.
30	the seam needs a real schema or tool, not files — the standalone-markdown premise is wrong: stop
31	and re-shape the seam.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## How to read this plan top-down
36	
37	Three layers, each mapping to one tracker artefact. Read outward from the bet above:
38	
39	```
40	initiative (this README)            ← goal + KRs
41	└── deliverable  D*/_deliverable.md  → milestone   (tagged serves_kr)
42	    └── node  N*.md                   → issue        (polymorphic: spike/story/adr/experiment/ktlo/capability/…)
43	        └── task  - [ ] in node        → sub-issue    (`skeleton` task opens the path; `acceptance` task closes it)
44	```
45	
46	Directory nesting **is** the hierarchy; numeric `D*/N*` prefixes give deterministic ordering.
47	Cross-references are relative paths plus front-matter `parent` / `serves_kr` back-links — so a
48	human descends by clicking and a script walks by reading front-matter. The schema is specified in
49	[`docs/delivery-shape-contract.md`](../../../docs/delivery-shape-contract.md).
50	
51	## Tree
52	
53	```
54	top-down-delivery-planning/
55	├── README.md                                              ← you are here (initiative root)
56	├── D1-walking-skeleton-spike-and-conversion-proof/        → milestone · serves KR1
57	│   ├── _deliverable.md
58	│   ├── N01 … hand-produce file-set + read off contract       · spike · skeleton
59	│   ├── N02 … walk-script: file-set → manifest                · story
60	│   └── N03 … ADR: new skill vs expand task-breakdown         · adr
61	├── D2-delivery-shape-skill-framing-baked-in/              → milestone · serves KR2
62	│   ├── _deliverable.md
63	│   ├── N04 … decompose, AC by default                        · story
64	│   ├── N05 … foundational prompt folded into skeleton        · story
65	│   ├── N06 … Rule A1 branch + up/down delegation             · story
66	│   └── N07 … self-trial against 2 initiatives                · experiment · [acceptance]
67	└── D3-trigger-reliability-and-discoverability/           → milestone · serves KR3
68	    ├── _deliverable.md
69	    ├── N08 … trigger-eval set + harness, 0 collisions        · story
70	    └── N09 … register in README + flowchart                  · ktlo
71	```
72	
73	## Node-type coverage (grounded — not fabricated)
74	
75	Nodes are **polymorphic**: each carries the completion criterion its work calls for, not always a
76	story. This example genuinely exercises five node types. The types it does *not* exercise are not
77	invented here — they live in the contract's to-fill appendix, to be grounded when an initiative
78	that uses them is shaped.
79	
80	| Type | Completion-criterion form | Exercised by |
81	|------|---------------------------|--------------|
82	| `spike` | decision + stop condition | N01 |
83	| `story` | acceptance criteria (Cohn form) | N02, N04, N05, N06, N08 |
84	| `adr` | accepted decision record | N03 |
85	| `experiment` | hypothesis + success metric | N07 |
86	| `ktlo` | none (roadmap A5 carve-out) | N09 |
87	| _capability, slo, migration, incident, deprecation, compliance_ | _see contract appendix_ | _not exercised by this initiative_ |
88	
89	`capability` is a genuine node `type` (completion form `the-capability-spec`), but this initiative
90	exercises none: every capability here was reducible to its child nodes and was absorbed into the
91	deliverable prose (see the contract's *Design notes*). It grounds when a capability carries a spec
92	its children don't.
93	
94	**Flags** (orthogonal to type — applied on top of any node type):
95	
96	| Flag | Forms | When it applies |
97	|------|-------|-----------------|
98	| `skeleton` | front-matter `skeleton: true` + task tag `` `skeleton` `` | Opens the end-to-end path; foundational work folded in |
99	| `acceptance` | front-matter `acceptance: true` + task tag `` `acceptance` `` | Closes the parent's cross-seam criterion. Exists only when parent's Done is irreducible to ∀child.done. Never re-runs child criteria. |
100	
101	`acceptance` in this plan: **N07** carries `acceptance: true` (verifies D2). Its experiment finding
102	— confirmed or falsified — is D2's aggregate Done condition (KR2 observed). The acceptance task
103	closes last, making D2's milestone reaching 100% coincide with the KR observation.
104	
105	## Hand-count manifest
106	
107	The mechanical-conversion proof (gate issue ABA-282) requires `bin/walk-delivery-plan` to emit
108	counts equal to these hand-counted totals:
109

113	| Issues | nodes (`N*`) | **9** |
114	| Sub-issues | tasks (`- [ ]` / `- [x]` lines) | **19** |

116	If the walk-script prints anything other than `3 / 9 / 19`, either the file-set drifted from this
117	count or the schema doesn't walk deterministically — investigate before declaring the gate passed.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""check-plan-framing — assert a delivery plan's framing was baked in, not dropped.
3	
4	Walks a delivery-plan file-set laid out per `docs/delivery-shape-contract.md`
5	and checks the framing the `delivery-shape` skill is supposed to emit *by
6	default*. This is the framing gate; it is orthogonal to `bin/walk-delivery-plan`
7	(which checks structural walkability + manifest counts). The two run side by
8	side: walk-script proves the plan converts to a manifest, this proves the plan
9	carries its completion framing.
10	
11	Four framing checks are implemented, each guarding a piece of framing the skill
12	must emit by default rather than the user re-prompting for:
13	
14	  1. Five body sections — every node carries the five headings: What, Why,
15	     Completion, Assumptions, Key Risks (in any order; presence is the gate).
16	     A node missing any heading fails and names the absent section(s). This
17	     replaces the earlier story-only acceptance-criteria check: the uniform
18	     template applies to all node types (Completion content varies by type;
19	     the heading is required on all of them).
20	
21	  2. Assumption tags — every list item under a node's `## Assumptions` heading
22	     carries a `(verified)` or `(to-verify)` tag anywhere in the line. An
23	     item without a tag is an untested claim being treated as a known fact.
24	     An empty Assumptions section (no list items, e.g. `*(none)*`) passes
25	     trivially — the tag rule only applies to explicit list items.
26	
27	  3. Foundational work folded into the skeleton — the plan carries at least one
28	     `` `skeleton` ``-flagged task, and no node places any task *before* its
29	     first skeleton task. Foundational / toolchain work belongs folded into the
30	     skeleton task's description; a task that precedes the skeleton is a setup
31	     task in disguise, deferring the integration discovery the skeleton exists
32	     to surface on day one. The pre-skeleton check is structural, not
33	     keyword-based: any task before the first skeleton task fails, whatever it
34	     is named — that is the only deterministic reading of "no setup task first."
35	
36	  4. Model annotations on every task — every task line (`` - [ ] ``) must contain
37	     a `Model:` annotation somewhere in the task text. This ensures each task
38	     explicitly names the model (e.g., Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) or tool that will
39	     execute it, preventing ambiguous task assignment.
40	
41	Like the walk-script, this reader is deliberately dependency-free (stdlib only,
42	no YAML library): it needs just two front-matter keys (`layer`, `type`), a
43	heading scan, and the walk-script's task-line *regex* (`TASK_RE`) — so a
44	targeted reader is more boring, and more honest about what it relies on, than
45	pulling in a parser. Headings and list items inside fenced code blocks are
46	literal text, not structure — the scanner skips them, consistent across all
47	three checks.
48	
49	Usage:
50	    bin/check-plan-framing <plan-dir> [--json]
51	
52	Exit codes:
53	    0   every node carries the five sections; no untagged assumption items;
54	        >=1 skeleton task; no node has a task before its skeleton; every task
55	        carries a Model: annotation
56	    1   a framing check failed: a node is missing a section, an assumption item
57	        lacks a tag, the plan has no skeleton task, a node places a task
58	        before its skeleton, or a task lacks a Model: annotation
59	    2   a node could not be parsed / no nodes found (seam not mechanical)
60	    64  usage error
61	"""
62	
63	from __future__ import annotations
64	
65	import json
66	import re
67	import sys
68	from pathlib import Path
69	
70	# --- schema constants (read off docs/delivery-shape-contract.md) -------------
71	
72	DELIVERABLE_DIR_RE = re.compile(r"^D(\d+)-")
73	NODE_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"^N(\d+)-.*\.md$")
74	HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$")  # ATX headings at column 0 (the contract emits them there)
75	LIST_ITEM_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s+\S")
76	FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(```|~~~)")
77	TASK_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*- \[([ xX])\]\s*(.*)$")  # same task grammar as walk-delivery-plan
78	SKELETON_TAG = "`skeleton`"
79	
80	# Five body sections required on every node (order-independent; presence is the gate).
81	REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ("What", "Why", "Completion", "Assumptions", "Key Risks")
82	REQUIRED_SECTION_RES = tuple(
83	    re.compile(rf"^{re.escape(s)}$", re.IGNORECASE) for s in REQUIRED_SECTIONS
84	)
85	
86	# Assumption-tag check — every list item under ## Assumptions must contain one.
87	# Matches `(verified)`, `(verified — explanation)`, `(to-verify)`, `(to-verify — explanation)`.
88	ASSUMPTION_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"\((verified|to-verify)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
89	ASSUMPTIONS_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^assumptions$", re.IGNORECASE)
90	
91	
92	class PlanError(Exception):
93	    """A structural / parse failure: the file-set does not read mechanically."""
94	
95	
96	# --- front-matter reader -----------------------------------------------------
97	
98	def _dequote(value: str) -> str:
99	    if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in "\"'":
100	        return value[1:-1]
101	    return value
102	
103	
104	def split_front_matter(path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]:
105	    """Return (front-matter scalars, body lines after the closing fence)."""
106	    try:
107	        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
108	    except OSError as exc:
109	        raise PlanError(f"{path}: cannot read ({exc})") from exc
110	
111	    if not lines or lines[0].strip() != "---":
112	        raise PlanError(f"{path}: missing opening '---' front-matter fence")
113	    end = next((i for i in range(1, len(lines)) if lines[i].strip() == "---"), None)
114	    if end is None:
115	        raise PlanError(f"{path}: front-matter fence not closed with '---'")
116	
117	    fm: dict[str, str] = {}
118	    for line in lines[1:end]:
119	        m = re.match(r"^([A-Za-z_][\w]*):(?:[ \t]+(.*))?$", line)
120	        if m and m.group(2):
121	            value = m.group(2).strip()
122	            if value not in (">", "|"):
123	                fm[m.group(1)] = _dequote(value)
124	    return fm, lines[end + 1:]
125	
126	
127	def missing_five_sections(body: list[str]) -> list[str]:
128	    """Return the required section headings absent from the body.
129	
130	    Checks only headings outside fenced code blocks (a heading inside a code
131	    block is literal text, not structure).
132	    """
133	    found: set[str] = set()
134	    in_fence = False
135	    for line in body:
136	        if FENCE_RE.match(line):
137	            in_fence = not in_fence
138	            continue
139	        if in_fence:
140	            continue
141	        m = HEADING_RE.match(line)
142	        if not m:
143	            continue
144	        text = m.group(1).strip()
145	        for name, section_re in zip(REQUIRED_SECTIONS, REQUIRED_SECTION_RES):
146	            if section_re.match(text):
147	                found.add(name)
148	    return [s for s in REQUIRED_SECTIONS if s not in found]
149	
150	
151	def untagged_assumptions(body: list[str]) -> list[str]:
152	    """Return Assumptions list items that lack a (verified) or (to-verify) tag.
153	
154	    Reads only the `## Assumptions` section (heading to next same-or-shallower
155	    heading). An empty section (no list items) passes trivially.
156	    """
157	    in_block = False
158	    in_fence = False
159	    block_level = 0
160	    violations: list[str] = []
161	    for line in body:
162	        if FENCE_RE.match(line):
163	            in_fence = not in_fence
164	            continue
165	        if in_fence:
166	            continue
167	        m = HEADING_RE.match(line)
168	        if m:
169	            level = len(line) - len(line.lstrip("#"))
170	            if ASSUMPTIONS_HEADING_RE.match(m.group(1).strip()):
171	                in_block = True
172	                block_level = level
173	                continue
174	            if in_block and level <= block_level:
175	                in_block = False
176	            continue
177	        if in_block and LIST_ITEM_RE.match(line):
178	            if not ASSUMPTION_TAG_RE.search(line):
179	                violations.append(line.strip())
180	    return violations
181	
182	
183	def read_tasks(body: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
184	    """Return the node's checklist tasks in order: [{skeleton: bool, has_model: bool, text: str}].
185	
186	    Matches the walk-script's task-line regex (`TASK_RE`). Task lines inside a
187	    fenced code block are literal text (e.g. a template in a SKILL), not plan
188	    structure, so they are skipped. Each task dict records whether the task
189	    text contains the `Model:` annotation.
190	    """
191	    tasks: list[dict] = []
192	    in_fence = False
193	    for line in body:
194	        if FENCE_RE.match(line):
195	            in_fence = not in_fence
196	            continue
197	        if in_fence:
198	            continue
199	        m = TASK_RE.match(line)
200	        if not m:
201	            continue
202	        text = m.group(2).strip()
203	        tasks.append({
204	            "skeleton": text.startswith(SKELETON_TAG),
205	            "has_model": "Model:" in text,
206	            "text": text
207	        })
208	    return tasks
209	
210	
211	# --- walk --------------------------------------------------------------------
212	
213	def _order(pattern: re.Pattern, name: str) -> int:
214	    m = pattern.match(name)
215	    return int(m.group(1)) if m else 0
216	
217	
218	def collect_nodes(root: Path) -> list[dict]:
219	    """Find every node and record its type, section presence, assumption tags, and tasks.
220	
221	    Walks the same deliverable→node layout as the walk-script. Each record
222	    carries enough for all four framing sub-checks.
223	    """
224	    deliverable_dirs = sorted(
225	        (d for d in root.iterdir() if d.is_dir() and DELIVERABLE_DIR_RE.match(d.name)),
226	        key=lambda d: _order(DELIVERABLE_DIR_RE, d.name),
227	    )
228	    if not deliverable_dirs:
229	        raise PlanError(f"{root}: no deliverable directories (D<n>-*) found")
230	
231	    node_files: list[Path] = []
232	    for ddir in deliverable_dirs:
233	        node_files.extend(sorted(
234	            (f for f in ddir.iterdir() if NODE_FILE_RE.match(f.name)),
235	            key=lambda f: _order(NODE_FILE_RE, f.name),
236	        ))
237	    if not node_files:
238	        raise PlanError(f"{root}: no node files (N<nn>-*.md) found")
239	
240	    nodes: list[dict] = []
241	    for nfile in node_files:
242	        fm, body = split_front_matter(nfile)
243	        if fm.get("layer") != "node":
244	            raise PlanError(f"{nfile}: layer is not 'node'")
245	        if "type" not in fm:
246	            raise PlanError(f"{nfile}: node missing required front-matter 'type'")
247	        tasks = read_tasks(body)
248	        nodes.append({
249	            "id": fm.get("id", nfile.stem),
250	            "path": str(nfile.relative_to(root)),
251	            "type": fm["type"],
252	            "missing_sections": missing_five_sections(body),
253	            "assumption_violations": untagged_assumptions(body),
254	            "missing_model": [t["text"] for t in tasks if not t["has_model"]],
255	            "tasks": tasks,
256	        })
257	    return nodes
258	
259	
260	def pre_skeleton_tasks(node: dict) -> list[str]:
261	    """Tasks that precede the node's first skeleton task — empty if none/no skeleton.
262	
263	    A node with no skeleton task has nothing for a task to be "pre" to, so it
264	    never contributes a violation (plan-level "at least one skeleton" is checked
265	    separately). When a skeleton task exists, every task before it is a
266	    pre-skeleton setup task, whatever it is named.
267	    """
268	    tasks = node["tasks"]
269	    first = next((i for i, t in enumerate(tasks) if t["skeleton"]), None)
270	    if first is None or first == 0:
271	        return []
272	    return [t["text"] for t in tasks[:first]]
273	
274	
275	def missing_model_annotations(node: dict) -> list[str]:
276	    """Tasks that lack a Model: annotation — empty if all carry one.
277	
278	    A task must contain `Model:` anywhere in its text to specify which model
279	    or tool will execute it.
280	    """
281	    return [t["text"] for t in node["tasks"] if not t["has_model"]]
282	
283	
284	# --- entrypoint --------------------------------------------------------------
285	
286	def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
287	    args = [a for a in argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
288	    as_json = "--json" in argv[1:]
289	    if len(args) != 1:
290	        sys.stderr.write("usage: check-plan-framing <plan-dir> [--json]\n")
291	        return 64
292	    root = Path(args[0])
293	    if not root.is_dir():
294	        sys.stderr.write(f"error: {root} is not a directory\n")
295	        return 64
296	
297	    try:
298	        nodes = collect_nodes(root)
299	    except PlanError as exc:
300	        sys.stderr.write(f"PARSE ERROR: {exc}\n")
301	        return 2
302	
303	    nodes_missing = [n for n in nodes if n["missing_sections"]]
304	    nodes_untagged = [n for n in nodes if n["assumption_violations"]]
305	    nodes_missing_model = [n for n in nodes if n["missing_model"]]
306	
307	    skeleton_total = sum(1 for n in nodes for t in n["tasks"] if t["skeleton"])
308	    no_skeleton = skeleton_total == 0
309	    pre_skeleton = [
310	        {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "tasks": pre}
311	        for n in nodes if (pre := pre_skeleton_tasks(n))
312	    ]
313	
314	    ok = not nodes_missing and not nodes_untagged and not no_skeleton and not pre_skeleton and not nodes_missing_model
315	
316	    if as_json:
317	        print(json.dumps({
318	            "source": str(root),
319	            "nodes_checked": len(nodes),
320	            "missing_sections": [
321	                {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "type": n["type"], "missing": n["missing_sections"]}
322	                for n in nodes_missing
323	            ],
324	            "untagged_assumptions": [
325	                {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "type": n["type"], "items": n["assumption_violations"]}
326	                for n in nodes_untagged
327	            ],
328	            "skeleton_tasks": skeleton_total,
329	            "pre_skeleton_setup": [
330	                {"id": p["id"], "path": p["path"], "tasks": p["tasks"]} for p in pre_skeleton
331	            ],
332	            "missing_model_annotations": [
333	                {"id": n["id"], "path": n["path"], "type": n["type"], "tasks": n["missing_model"]} for n in nodes_missing_model
334	            ],
335	            "ok": ok,
336	        }, indent=2))
337	    else:
338	        print(f"check-plan-framing — {root.name}")
339	        print(f"source: {root}")
340	        print(f"nodes checked: {len(nodes)}")
341	        for n in nodes:
342	            if n["missing_sections"]:
343	                missing_str = ", ".join(n["missing_sections"])
344	                print(f"  [MISSING {missing_str}] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
345	            elif n["assumption_violations"]:
346	                print(f"  [UNTAGGED ASSUMPTION] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
347	            elif n["missing_model"]:
348	                print(f"  [MISSING MODEL] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
349	            else:
350	                print(f"  [ok ] {n['id']}  {n['path']}  ({n['type']})")
351	        print(f"skeleton tasks in plan: {skeleton_total}")
352	        for p in pre_skeleton:
353	            print(f"  [PRE-SKELETON] {p['id']}  {p['path']}: {len(p['tasks'])} task(s) before skeleton")
354	        for m in nodes_missing_model:
355	            print(f"  [MISSING MODEL] {m['id']}  {m['path']}: {len(m['tasks'])} task(s) without Model: annotation")
356	        verdict = (
357	            "PASS — five sections, assumption tags, skeleton task, no pre-skeleton setup, Model: annotations"
358	            if ok else
359	            "FAIL — " + "; ".join(filter(None, [
360	                f"{len(nodes_missing)} node(s) missing required sections" if nodes_missing else "",
361	                f"{len(nodes_untagged)} node(s) with untagged assumption items" if nodes_untagged else "",
362	                "no skeleton task in plan" if no_skeleton else "",
363	                f"{len(pre_skeleton)} node(s) with a task before the skeleton" if pre_skeleton else "",
364	                f"{len(nodes_missing_model)} node(s) with tasks lacking Model: annotation" if nodes_missing_model else "",
365	            ]))
366	        )
367	        print(verdict)
368	
369	    if not ok:
370	        sys.stderr.write("\nFRAMING DROPPED:\n")
371	        if nodes_missing:
372	            sys.stderr.write(
373	                "  nodes missing one or more of the five required body sections "
374	                "(What / Why / Completion / Assumptions / Key Risks):\n"
375	                + "".join(
376	                    f"    - {n['path']}  missing: {', '.join(n['missing_sections'])}\n"
377	                    for n in nodes_missing
378	                )
379	            )
380	        if nodes_untagged:
381	            sys.stderr.write(
382	                "  Assumptions list items without a (verified) or (to-verify) tag — "
383	                "every assumption must be explicitly verified or marked for verification:\n"
384	                + "".join(
385	                    f"    - {n['path']}:\n"
386	                    + "".join(f"        {item}\n" for item in n["assumption_violations"])
387	                    for n in nodes_untagged
388	                )
389	            )
390	        if no_skeleton:
391	            sys.stderr.write(
392	                "  the plan carries no `skeleton`-flagged task — at least one node must mark its "
393	                "thinnest end-to-end slice with a leading `skeleton` tag, foundational work folded in.\n"
394	            )
395	        if pre_skeleton:
396	            sys.stderr.write(
397	                "  nodes that place a task before their skeleton — the skeleton must be the first "
398	                "task; if the preceding task is setup/toolchain work, fold it into the skeleton's "
399	                "description rather than emitting it before:\n"
400	                + "".join(
401	                    f"    - {p['path']}: " + " | ".join(p["tasks"]) + "\n"
402	                    for p in pre_skeleton
403	                )
404	            )
405	        if nodes_missing_model:
406	            sys.stderr.write(
407	                "  tasks without a Model: annotation — every task must explicitly specify which "
408	                "model or tool will execute it:\n"
409	                + "".join(
410	                    f"    - {n['path']}:\n"
411	                    + "".join(f"        {task}\n" for task in n["missing_model"])
412	                    for n in nodes_missing_model
413	                )
414	            )
415	        return 1
416	    return 0
417	
418	
419	if __name__ == "__main__":
420	    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))
421	
```

  "content": "---\nlayer: node\nid: N01\ntype: story\ntitle: Fixture corpus + review grader\nparent: D1\nserves_kr: KR2\nmaps_to: linear-issue\nskeleton: true\nexternal_window: none\ncompletion:\n  form: acceptance-criteria\n  criterion: >\n    bin/grade-execution-review runs every persona prompt file against every fixture\n    diff and scores surfaced findings against a seeded manifest of 10\n    Critical/Required findings across ≥3 defect classes, caching run logs.\ndelegates_to: at-pickup task breakdown (story); grader discipline mirrors bin/walk-delivery-plan (stdlib-only, deterministic)\n---\n\n# N01 — Fixture corpus + review grader\n\n**Type:** `story` · **Walking skeleton of the whole initiative** (`skeleton: true`).\n\n> **▶ On pickup:** break this node into build tasks per the at-pickup breakdown; the grader\n> follows the same stdlib-only, deterministic-reader discipline as `bin/walk-delivery-plan`.\n\n## What\n\nAs a skill author hardening the review gate, I want a fixture corpus of diffs with seeded defects\nand a grader that scores any persona against them, so that review quality is measured against a\nknown answer key instead of eyeballed. The corpus lives at `fixtures/execution-review/` — one\nfixture diff + one seeded-finding manifest per fixture — and `bin/grade-execution-review` runs\neach persona over each diff, diffs surfaced findings against the manifest, and caches the run\nunder `fixtures/execution-review/_runs/`.\n\n## Why\n\nThe bet: building the harness *before* the personas makes KR2 falsifiable from day one and gives\nevery later persona edit a regression gate instead of a vibe check. Rejected alternative: author\nthe personas first and grade their output by inspection — no answer key, KR2 unfalsifiable, and\npersona quality drifts invisibly with each edit. This node is the initiative's walking skeleton:\nit exercises the fixture → persona-run → grade seam end-to-end with a stub persona before any\nreal persona exists, surfacing the finding-matching problem (the riskiest part of D1) on day one.\nIt unlocks N03's iterate-to-≥9/10 loop.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** `bin/grade-execution-review fixtures/execution-review/` runs every persona\n  prompt file it finds against every fixture diff and reports surfaced vs seeded findings with a\n  deterministic exit code.\n- **Done when:** the corpus seeds 10 Critical/Required findings across ≥3 defect classes (type\n  suppression, AC violation, security hole).\n- **Done when:** each run's log is cached under `fixtures/execution-review/_runs/`.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Seeded-defect diffs can be authored as static fixture files without a live repo to apply them to. *(verified — the graded artefact is the persona's reading of a diff, not a build)*\n- A stdlib-only grader can match persona findings to manifest entries deterministically. *(to-verify — matching free-prose findings to seeded entries is the spike-shaped corner of this node; the structured finding format N02 pins is the intended fix)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** finding-to-manifest matching is too fuzzy and the grader over- or under-credits\n  personas, making the ≥9/10 gate meaningless.\n  *Mitigation:* require personas to emit findings in the structured line format the N02 contract\n  pins (file · defect class · severity), so matching is exact key comparison, not prose fuzzing.\n- **Risk:** seeded defects are too easy, and 9/10 is reachable by a weak persona — false\n  confidence in the gate.\n  *Falsifier:* a deliberately weak stub persona scores ≥9/10. If it does, harden the corpus\n  before grading any real persona.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Seed one fixture diff with a 3-finding manifest and run a stub persona through `bin/grade-execution-review` end-to-end (fixture layout, grader scaffold, and `_runs/` cache folded in) · Done when: the grader exits 0 reporting 3/3 for an oracle stub and non-zero for an empty stub · Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Grow the corpus to 10 seeded Critical/Required findings across ≥3 defect classes (type suppression, AC violation, security hole) · Done when: the manifest lists 10 findings across ≥3 classes and the weak-stub falsifier scores below 9/10 · Model: Fast · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Document the grading protocol (run, cache, read results) in the fixture-set README · Done when: a fresh agent can run the grader and interpret a score from the README alone · Model: Fast · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = L·L·L·L·L\n"

  "content": "---\nlayer: node\nid: N06\ntype: story\ntitle: \"Build skill: RED/GREEN/commit loop\"\nparent: D2\nserves_kr: KR1\nmaps_to: linear-issue\nexternal_window: none\ncompletion:\n  form: acceptance-criteria\n  criterion: >\n    A build skill exists enforcing a gated RED → GREEN → commit loop per slice, with a\n    verification-form fallback for non-code repos and a named escalation path into the\n    debugging skill.\ndelegates_to: at-pickup task breakdown (story); authoring per docs/skill-anatomy.md\n---\n\n# N06 — Build skill: RED/GREEN/commit loop\n\n**Type:** `story`.\n\n> **Blocked by:** [N04](N04-execution-workflow-design-doc.md) — task breakdown waits until the\n> design doc is accepted.\n\n> **▶ On pickup:** break into build tasks per the at-pickup breakdown; author per\n> `docs/skill-anatomy.md` against the accepted N04 contract.\n\n## What\n\nAs a worker building a broken-down task, I want a gated RED/GREEN/commit loop, so that every\nincrement lands verified, smallest-first, with a commit trail a reviewer can replay. The loop is\nper slice: a failing check first (RED), the minimal change that passes it (GREEN), one commit —\nwith `[GATE]` markers that are not optional.\n\n## Why\n\nThe bet: the gated TDD loop is the discipline both external packs converged on independently\n(superpowers' per-task implementer loop; agent-skills' /build RED/GREEN/commit) — convergent\nevolution is the strongest signal in the deep review. Rejected alternative: advisory\n\"write tests first\" prose without gates — advisory prose is precisely what a worker under token\npressure skips, and ungated discipline is the failure mode the pack's `[GATE]` convention exists\nto prevent.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the skill enforces RED (failing check first) → GREEN (minimal pass) → commit per\n  slice, with `[GATE]` markers.\n- **Done when:** a verification-form fallback exists for repos with no test runner, chosen at\n  breakdown time (gate script, grader, link check — a deterministic check, not necessarily a\n  unit test).\n- **Done when:** a named escalation path into the debugging skill (N07) replaces retry-flailing\n  after consecutive red loops.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Drained repos expose a runnable verification command discoverable from repo instructions. *(to-verify — markdown-only repos like Shaper itself are the hard case; the verification-form fallback is the intended answer and the first validation drain checks it)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** in markdown-only repos RED/GREEN reads as meaningless and workers skip the skill\n  wholesale.\n  *Mitigation:* the verification-form fallback redefines RED as \"the deterministic check fails\"\n  (e.g. `bin/check-plan-framing` non-zero) so the loop is exercised identically; the fallback is\n  selected at breakdown time, not improvised mid-build.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the RED/GREEN/commit loop core with its gates and the per-slice commit convention (skill dir + frontmatter folded in) · Done when: the skill passes anatomy section order and the loop's gates are marked `[GATE]` · Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Write the verification-form fallback and the consecutive-failure escalation into the debugging skill · Done when: both paths are named delegations selectable at breakdown time · Model: Fast · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Trial the loop on one toy task and record the transcript as the skill's worked example · Done when: the transcript shows RED → GREEN → commit with no skipped gate · Model: Fast · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = L·L·L·L·L\n"
}

These are the two\ndomain skills confirmed in at the interview (frontend/perf/browser explicitly out).\n\n## Why\n\nThe bet: the two failure modes that most often force a human rescue mid-drain are undiagnosed\nfailures (worker loops on retries) and over-built diffs (reviewer drowns) — these skills target\nexactly those, which is why they made the shortlist and the rest didn't. Rejected alternative:\nkeep superpowers installed for its debugging skill alone — that keeps the third-party dependency\nalive and makes KR3's uninstall impossible.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the debugging skill encodes hypothesis → instrument → bisect → fix with a\n  written root-cause note as a gate (no fix without a stated cause).\n- **Done when:** the simplification skill runs as a post-green pass emitting a reviewable\n  before/after rationale.\n- **Done when:** both are reachable by name from the build skill's escalation and exit points.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Two skills (not one) is the right split — debugging fires mid-loop, simplification fires post-green. *(verified — they occupy different trigger points in the N04 graph; folding them would blur both triggers)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** accidental verbatim port of superpowers' debugging prose — a predecessor-rule\n  violation.\n  *Mitigation:* frontmatter declares the predecessor relation; voice check against two existing\n  pack skills at review, per repo convention.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the systematic-debugging skill with the root-cause-note gate (skill dir + frontmatter folded in) · Done when: the skill passes anatomy order and the no-fix-without-stated-cause gate is marked `[GATE]` · Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Author the simplification skill as a post-green pass with before/after rationale · Done when: the skill emits a reviewable simplification note on a sample diff · Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Wire both into the build skill's escalation and exit points by name · Done when: the build skill names both delegations and neither is inlined · Model: Fast · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = L·L·L·L·L\n"

Consumes the review-summary produced by\n> [N03](../D1-review-gate-proven-on-seeded-defects/N03-personas-and-review-fan-out.md).\n\n> **▶ On pickup:** break into build tasks per the at-pickup breakdown; verify the gt command\n> surface against current Graphite docs before relying on it (the HS companion below).\n\n## What\n\nAs a worker with a verified diff, I want a Graphite-first PR finishing skill with a plain-git\nfallback, so that every drain ends in a stacked, reviewable PR carrying a What/Why/Focus body and\na review-summary comment instead of an unreviewed push. The trail artefacts this skill emits are\nexactly what KR1's \"full review trail\" check greps for.\n\n## Why\n\nThe bet: Graphite-first matches the owner's tooling and drain-cycle's half-built stack mode\n(`.drain-handoff.json`), so stacking works where it matters without stranding environments that\nlack `gt`. Rejected alternatives, both directions: plain-git-only (works everywhere but abandons\nstacking — the reason Graphite is in the stack at all) and Graphite-only (breaks any repo or\nworker without gt installed). Per-repo push policy (direct-to-main vs PR) stays with repo\ninstructions; the skill honours it rather than overriding it.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the skill detects `gt` and submits a stacked PR; when absent, the plain-git path\n  produces a branch + PR with the identical body/trail contract.\n- **Done when:** every finish lands the What/Why/Focus PR body and posts the review-summary\n  comment to the Linear issue.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The gt command surface used (branch create / submit) is stable across the versions where workers run. *(to-verify — pin the verified command set during authoring; the source-driven-development companion fires on the skeleton task)*\n- Per-repo push policy is readable from repo instructions. *(verified — this repo's AGENTS.md states it; the skill reads, not assumes)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** the Graphite and git paths drift — different bodies or trail artefacts — making\n  KR1's trail check flaky depending on which path ran.\n  *Mitigation:* one shared body/trail template both paths fill; the fallback task's Done-when\n  asserts artefact parity, not just \"a PR exists\".\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the Graphite-first flow (gt detection → branch → stacked submit) with the What/Why/Focus body template (skill dir + shared trail template folded in) · Done when: a toy diff lands as a stacked PR with the body contract filled · Model: Balanced · risk reversible · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·H·M·L · companions source-driven-development\n- [ ] Write the plain-git fallback with trail parity · Done when: the same toy diff finished via the fallback yields identical body and trail artefacts · Model: Fast · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·M·L·L\n- [ ] Write the review-summary comment + Linear status update step · Done when: the issue shows the review-summary comment and status moves per governance at the moment of state change · Model: Fast · risk reversible · review standard · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = L·L·L·L·L\n"

  "description": "`story` · serves **KR2** · **walking skeleton of the whole initiative**\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); grader discipline mirrors `bin/walk-delivery-plan` (stdlib-only, deterministic).\n\n## What\n\nAs a skill author hardening the review gate, I want a fixture corpus of diffs with seeded defects and a grader that scores any persona against them, so that review quality is measured against a known answer key instead of eyeballed. Corpus at `fixtures/execution-review/` (one diff + one seeded-finding manifest per fixture); `bin/grade-execution-review` runs each persona over each diff and caches runs under `fixtures/execution-review/_runs/`.\n\n## Why\n\nHarness before personas makes KR2 falsifiable from day one and gives every persona edit a regression gate. Rejected alternative: author personas first and grade by inspection — no answer key, KR2 unfalsifiable. As the walking skeleton it exercises fixture → persona-run → grade end-to-end with a stub persona, surfacing the finding-matching problem (D1's riskiest part) on day one.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** `bin/grade-execution-review fixtures/execution-review/` runs every persona prompt file against every fixture diff and reports surfaced vs seeded findings with a deterministic exit code.\n- **Done when:** the corpus seeds 10 Critical/Required findings across ≥3 defect classes (type suppression, AC violation, security hole).\n- **Done when:** each run's log is cached under `fixtures/execution-review/_runs/`.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Seeded-defect diffs can be static fixture files, no live repo needed *(verified — the graded artefact is the persona's reading of a diff, not a build)*\n- A stdlib-only grader can match findings to manifest entries deterministically *(to-verify — the structured finding format N02 pins is the intended fix)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** finding-to-manifest matching too fuzzy → ≥9/10 gate meaningless. *Mitigation:* personas emit the structured line format the N02 contract pins (file · defect class · severity); matching is exact key comparison.\n- **Risk:** seeded defects too easy → false confidence. *Falsifier:* a deliberately weak stub persona scores ≥9/10 — if so, harden the corpus first.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Seed one fixture diff with a 3-finding manifest and run a stub persona through `bin/grade-execution-review` end-to-end (fixture layout, grader scaffold, `_runs/` cache folded in) · Done when: grader exits 0 reporting 3/3 for an oracle stub and non-zero for an empty stub · Model: Balanced · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Grow the corpus to 10 seeded Critical/Required findings across ≥3 defect classes · Done when: manifest lists 10 findings across ≥3 classes and the weak-stub falsifier scores <9/10 · Model: Fast · axes M·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Document the grading protocol in the fixture-set README · Done when: a fresh agent can run the grader and interpret a score from the README alone · Model: Fast · axes L·L·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N01](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D1-review-gate-proven-on-seeded-defects/N01-fixture-corpus-and-grader.md)"
}
```

Rejected alternative: Claude-Code-native agent definitions — richer dispatch but strands codex/kimi workers. ADR not design doc: single surface, bounded consequences, mechanical migration — Rule A1's \"a short ADR may suffice\" branch.\n\n## Completion\n\n**Decision:** open — recorded at pickup. The accepted record pins (a) persona file format + location, (b) the structured finding line (file · defect class · severity), (c) dispatch: Agent fan-out on Claude Code, inline-sequential fallback elsewhere — Context / Decision / Consequences, filed under `docs/adr/`.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The Agent tool can dispatch a plain prompt-file persona without a pack-native agent definition *(verified — the persona file's content is the prompt)*\n- A structured finding format does not depress persona recall vs free prose *(to-verify — checked against the N01 harness during N03's iteration)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** contract over-fits Claude Code; the non-Claude fallback is unusable, undermining initiative C. *Mitigation:* fallback written as plain prose in the same persona file, trialled once inline before the ADR is accepted.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] Record Context: enumerate dispatch surfaces (Claude Agent fan-out; codex/kimi inline-sequential) and ≥2 candidate contract shapes with trade-offs · Done when: Context names both surfaces and the candidates · Model: Frontier · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·H·L·M·L\n- [ ] Record Decision + Consequences (file format, finding format, dispatch + fallback); set status accepted · Done when: ADR accepted and N03 can author with no open contract questions · Model: Frontier · axes H·H·L·M·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N02](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D1-review-gate-proven-on-seeded-defects/N02-adr-persona-contract.md)"

N05–N08's task breakdown waits until this is accepted.\n\n## What\n\nThe design doc for the execution workflow: the verb namespace (the one-way door), the skill graph (pickup → breakdown-at-pickup → build → debug/simplify → review fan-out → verify → PR finishing), the inter-skill handoff contract — what each step receives and emits, including how the issue's acceptance criteria travel to the spec-compliance review lens — plus headless-first / vendor-portability constraints and persona-dispatch integration (per N02).\n\n## Why\n\nOne accepted design decides the namespace and the seams once, so five skills are authored against a stable contract. Rejected alternative: each skill defines its own interface ad hoc — incompatible handoffs, and a namespace chosen by accident becomes permanent the moment drain-cycle prompts bind to it. Unblocks N05–N08; gives initiative B a single naming table to consume.\n\n## Completion\n\nAn accepted design doc covering: verb namespace with rationale and rejected alternatives; skill graph + handoff contract; headless-first and non-Claude-worker constraints; persona-dispatch integration. Accepted through the `plan-review` gate.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Shaping verbs stay `shape:*`; only the execution verb is open *(verified — confirmed in the parked initiative shape)*\n- drain-cycle's verify-flow expectations (`/shape:task`, `/shape:verify-implementation`, `/shape:pr-prepare`, `/shape:pr-respond`) can be satisfied or migrated by the new graph *(to-verify — audit drain_cycle/prompt.py + verify flow at pickup, before pinning the namespace)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** verb collides with initiative B's consolidation naming, forcing a rename after habits form. *Mitigation:* the doc reserves both verb sets (shaping + execution) in one naming table; B consumes it — naming decided once, here.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] Frame problem + constraints and draft ≥2 alternatives for verb namespace and skill graph · Done when: doc presents alternatives with trade-offs against headless-first and vendor portability · Model: Frontier · risk one-way · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·H·L·H·L · companions code-review-and-quality\n- [ ] Record the decision + inter-skill handoff contract; pass the plan-review exit gate · Done when: doc accepted and N05–N08 can break tasks against it · Model: Frontier · risk one-way · review elevated · axes H·H·L·H·L · companions code-review-and-quality\n\n---\nPlan source: [N04](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N04-execution-workflow-design-doc.md)"

  "description": "`story` · serves **KR2** · blocked by N02 (the contract) · graded by N01's harness\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); authoring per `docs/skill-anatomy.md` and the accepted N02 contract.\n\n## What\n\nAs a drain-cycle worker finishing a build, I want a first-party review fan-out skill that dispatches code-reviewer, security-auditor, and spec-compliance personas over my diff and aggregates a GO/NO-GO verdict, so that every PR carries a multi-lens review trail with no third-party pack on the path. This replaces the hardcoded `/code-review-and-quality` dependency. Review order is fixed: spec compliance **before** code quality.\n\n## Why\n\nThree narrow lenses surface more of the seeded findings than one broad reviewer, and spec-first ordering catches built-the-wrong-thing before built-it-badly. Rejected alternative: port the third-party monolithic review skill verbatim — forbidden by the pack's predecessor rule, and a single lens leaves security/AC defect classes ungraded. Unlocks N05's review step; precondition for N11's uninstall.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** three persona prompt files exist per the N02 contract, each emitting structured-format findings.\n- **Done when:** the fan-out skill dispatches all three (Agent fan-out on Claude Code, inline-sequential fallback elsewhere) and aggregates one deduped GO/NO-GO verdict with a review-summary block.\n- **Done when:** `bin/grade-execution-review` reports ≥9/10 seeded findings surfaced — the KR2 observation.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The issue's acceptance criteria are available at review time for the spec-compliance lens *(to-verify — depends on the N04 handoff contract; trial interactively until then)*\n- ≥9/10 reachable with three personas *(to-verify — the iteration task exists for exactly this)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** persona findings overlap; aggregate double-counts and inflates the grade. *Mitigation:* grader and fan-out both dedupe on the contract's match key (file · defect class).\n- **Risk:** persona set plateaus below 9/10. *Falsifier:* two hardening iterations with per-class miss analysis fail to clear the bar — re-shape the persona split (KR2 is a commit).\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the code-reviewer persona to the N02 contract and dispatch it through a minimal fan-out skill against one fixture (skill scaffold + persona directory folded in) · Done when: the persona's findings flow through the fan-out path into the grader and score · Model: Balanced · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Author security-auditor + spec-compliance personas, spec-compliance reviewing AC before code quality · Done when: all three emit contract-format findings across the corpus · Model: Balanced · axes H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Aggregate the three verdicts into one deduped GO/NO-GO with a review-summary block ordered spec → security → quality · Done when: one invocation yields a single verdict artefact with no duplicate findings · Model: Fast · axes M·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Iterate the persona set against the harness with per-class miss analysis from `_runs/` logs · Done when: `bin/grade-execution-review` ≥9/10 · Model: Balanced · axes H·M·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N03](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D1-review-gate-proven-on-seeded-defects/N03-personas-and-review-fan-out.md)"
}

  "description": "`story` · serves **KR1** · blocked by N04 (task breakdown waits for the accepted design doc)\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); authoring per `docs/skill-anatomy.md` against the accepted N04 contract.\n\n## What\n\nAs a drain-cycle worker picking up a Linear issue, I want one front-door skill that takes me from pickup through breakdown-at-pickup, build, review, verify, and PR finishing, so that the supervisor prompt can be a single pointer and the whole procedure lives in the pack. This is the skill `drain_cycle/prompt.py` will point at (N10) — the keystone of the thin-supervisor architecture.\n\n## Why\n\nBreakdown-at-pickup on fresh context beats plan-time task expansion (detail decays before the node is reached), and one front door is what lets the supervisor prompt shrink to a pointer — the premise initiatives A and C share. Rejected alternative: a prompt-side checklist inside drain-cycle — workflow trapped in one vendor's supervisor, the exact coupling this initiative removes. Unblocks N10.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the skill exists per `docs/skill-anatomy.md`, walks the N04 graph with every step a *named delegation* to its owning skill, and carries the issue's acceptance criteria through the handoff contract to the review step.\n- **Done when:** a dry run on one real issue reaches the PR step without re-prompting.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Linear issue context (body, AC, labels) is available at pickup *(verified — drain-cycle injects issue context into the worktree prompt today)*\n- The five-section node body is sufficient input for at-pickup breakdown *(to-verify — checked on the first validation drain)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** the front door bloats into re-authored copies of the steps it orchestrates. *Mitigation:* P7 gate at review — every step a named delegation, no inlined procedure; ~150-line execution-skill target makes inlining structurally impossible.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the front door end-to-end with each workflow step a named delegation to the build, debug/simplify, review (N03), verify, and PR skills (skill dir + frontmatter folded in) · Done when: a toy-issue dry run reaches the PR step with every step delegated by name · Model: Balanced · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·M·L\n- [ ] Write the breakdown-at-pickup section: size check + Done-when clause on every build task · Done when: breakdown of a sample node yields tasks each carrying exactly one verifiable Done-when clause · Model: Balanced · axes H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Write the blocked/halt path per workflow governance: comment naming the blocker, issue stays In Progress, no false Done · Done when: dry run of a blocked issue ends with a Linear comment naming the blocker and unchanged status · Model: Fast · axes M·M·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N05](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N05-entry-skill-front-door.md)"
}

{
  "team": "Personal",
  "project": "f9399232-74f6-45fe-977c-dde359f2c035",
  "milestone": "D2 — Execution workflow drains issues end-to-end",
  "title": "N06 — Build skill: RED/GREEN/commit loop",
  "labels": [
    "agent-skills-shaper",
    "sonnet"
  ],
  "blockedBy": [
    "ABA-361"
  ],
  "description": "`story` · serves **KR1** · blocked by N04 (task breakdown waits for the accepted design doc)\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); authoring per `docs/skill-anatomy.md` against the accepted N04 contract.\n\n## What\n\nAs a worker building a broken-down task, I want a gated RED/GREEN/commit loop, so that every increment lands verified, smallest-first, with a commit trail a reviewer can replay. Per slice: a failing check first (RED), the minimal change that passes (GREEN), one commit — `[GATE]` markers non-optional.\n\n## Why\n\nThe gated TDD loop is the discipline both external packs converged on independently (superpowers' per-task implementer loop; agent-skills' /build) — convergent evolution is the strongest signal in the deep review. Rejected alternative: advisory \"write tests first\" prose without gates — precisely what a worker under token pressure skips.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the skill enforces RED → GREEN → commit per slice, with `[GATE]` markers.\n- **Done when:** a verification-form fallback exists for repos with no test runner, chosen at breakdown time (gate script, grader, link check — a deterministic check, not necessarily a unit test).\n- **Done when:** a named escalation path into the debugging skill (N07) replaces retry-flailing after consecutive red loops.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Drained repos expose a runnable verification command discoverable from repo instructions *(to-verify — markdown-only repos like Shaper itself are the hard case; the fallback is the intended answer, checked on the first validation drain)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** in markdown-only repos RED/GREEN reads as meaningless and workers skip the skill wholesale. *Mitigation:* the verification-form fallback redefines RED as \"the deterministic check fails\" (e.g. `bin/check-plan-framing` non-zero); fallback selected at breakdown time, not improvised mid-build.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the RED/GREEN/commit loop core with its gates and the per-slice commit convention (skill dir + frontmatter folded in) · Done when: skill passes anatomy section order and the loop's gates are marked `[GATE]` · Model: Balanced · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Write the verification-form fallback and the consecutive-failure escalation into the debugging skill · Done when: both paths are named delegations selectable at breakdown time · Model: Fast · axes M·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Trial the loop on one toy task and record the transcript as the skill's worked example · Done when: transcript shows RED → GREEN → commit with no skipped gate · Model: Fast · axes L·L·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N06](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N06-build-skill-red-green-commit.md)"
}

  "description": "`story` · serves **KR1** · blocked by N04 (task breakdown waits for the accepted design doc)\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); authoring per `docs/skill-anatomy.md`; declare each skill's predecessor relation in frontmatter (no verbatim ports).\n\n## What\n\nAs a worker stuck on a failing build or finishing a green one, I want systematic-debugging and simplification skills, so that failures resolve by hypothesis and evidence rather than retry-flailing, and green code sheds incidental complexity before review. The two domain skills confirmed at interview (frontend/perf/browser explicitly out).\n\n## Why\n\nThe two failure modes that most often force a human rescue mid-drain are undiagnosed failures (worker loops on retries) and over-built diffs (reviewer drowns) — these skills target exactly those. Rejected alternative: keep superpowers installed for its debugging skill alone — keeps the third-party dependency alive and makes KR3's uninstall impossible.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the debugging skill encodes hypothesis → instrument → bisect → fix with a written root-cause note as a gate (no fix without a stated cause).\n- **Done when:** the simplification skill runs as a post-green pass emitting a reviewable before/after rationale.\n- **Done when:** both are reachable by name from the build skill's escalation and exit points.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Two skills (not one) is the right split — debugging fires mid-loop, simplification post-green *(verified — different trigger points in the N04 graph; folding would blur both triggers)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** accidental verbatim port of superpowers' debugging prose — predecessor-rule violation. *Mitigation:* frontmatter declares the predecessor relation; voice check against two existing pack skills at review.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the systematic-debugging skill with the root-cause-note gate (skill dir + frontmatter folded in) · Done when: skill passes anatomy order and the no-fix-without-stated-cause gate is marked `[GATE]` · Model: Balanced · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Author the simplification skill as a post-green pass with before/after rationale · Done when: the skill emits a reviewable simplification note on a sample diff · Model: Balanced · axes H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Wire both into the build skill's escalation and exit points by name · Done when: the build skill names both delegations and neither is inlined · Model: Fast · axes L·L·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N07](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N07-debugging-and-simplification.md)"
}

  "description": "`story` · serves **KR1** · blocked by N04 (task breakdown waits for the accepted design doc) · consumes N03's review-summary\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); verify the gt command surface against current Graphite docs before relying on it (HS companion: source-driven-development).\n\n## What\n\nAs a worker with a verified diff, I want a Graphite-first PR finishing skill with a plain-git fallback, so that every drain ends in a stacked, reviewable PR carrying a What/Why/Focus body and a review-summary comment instead of an unreviewed push. The trail artefacts this skill emits are exactly what KR1's \"full review trail\" check greps for.\n\n## Why\n\nGraphite-first matches the owner's tooling and drain-cycle's half-built stack mode (`.drain-handoff.json`), so stacking works where it matters without stranding environments that lack `gt`. Rejected alternatives, both directions: plain-git-only (abandons stacking) and Graphite-only (breaks any repo or worker without gt). Per-repo push policy stays with repo instructions; the skill honours it.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the skill detects `gt` and submits a stacked PR; when absent, the plain-git path produces a branch + PR with the identical body/trail contract.\n- **Done when:** every finish lands the What/Why/Focus PR body and posts the review-summary comment to the Linear issue.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The gt command surface used (branch create / submit) is stable across worker environments *(to-verify — pin the verified command set during authoring; source-driven-development companion fires on the skeleton task)*\n- Per-repo push policy is readable from repo instructions *(verified — this repo's AGENTS.md states it)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** Graphite and git paths drift — different bodies or trail artefacts — making KR1's trail check flaky depending on path. *Mitigation:* one shared body/trail template both paths fill; the fallback task's Done-when asserts artefact parity.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the Graphite-first flow (gt detection → branch → stacked submit) with the What/Why/Focus body template (skill dir + shared trail template folded in) · Done when: a toy diff lands as a stacked PR with the body contract filled · Model: Balanced · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·H·M·L · companions source-driven-development\n- [ ] Write the plain-git fallback with trail parity · Done when: the same toy diff finished via the fallback yields identical body and trail artefacts · Model: Fast · axes M·M·M·L·L\n- [ ] Write the review-summary comment + Linear status update step · Done when: the issue shows the review-summary comment and status moves per governance at the moment of state change · Model: Fast · axes L·L·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N08](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N08-pr-finishing-graphite-first.md)"
}

Keep the diff to the pointer swap — the full prompt-template re-scope is initiative C's.\n\n## What\n\nAs the drain-cycle supervisor, I want my worker prompt to point at the pack's entry skill instead of inlining procedure and a third-party review skill, so that workers follow one source of truth and uninstalling agent-skills breaks nothing. Removes the hardcoded `/code-review-and-quality` dependency in `drain_cycle/prompt.py` — the uninstall blocker the deep review flagged.\n\n## Why\n\nA pointer is the smallest change that unblocks the uninstall (N11) and validates the thin-supervisor seam before initiative C invests in it. Rejected alternative: keep the inlined procedure as a parallel fallback — two sources of truth, and workers follow the stale one. Scope fence: pointer swap only; the ≤15-line template reform belongs to initiative C.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** `prompt.py` references the entry skill, `grep -rn 'code-review-and-quality' drain_cycle/` returns empty, and drain-cycle's pytest suite is green.\n- **Done when:** one smoke drain completes pickup → PR through the pointer with no inlined-procedure fallback.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The entry skill is visible to worker sessions drain-cycle spawns (`claude -p` in a worktree) *(to-verify — plugin/skill visibility under headless worktree sessions is the load-bearing unknown; the smoke-drain task checks it first)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** prompt change degrades worker behaviour mid-cycle. *Mitigation:* smoke-drain a low-stakes issue before validation drains start; the swap is one commit, reverted in one command — a two-way door.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Swap the inlined review/procedure reference in `prompt.py` for the entry-skill pointer (test updates folded in) · Done when: `grep -rn 'code-review-and-quality' drain_cycle/` is empty and pytest is green · Model: Fast · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·L·L·M·L\n- [ ] Run one smoke drain through the pointer on a low-stakes issue · Done when: the worker completes pickup → PR via the entry skill with no inlined-procedure fallback observed in the transcript · Model: Fast · axes M·M·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N10](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D3-cutover-off-third-party-packs/N10-drain-cycle-prompt-pointer.md)"

    "ABA-367"
