  "description": "`experiment` · serves **KR1** · **acceptance: verifies D2** — close LAST so the milestone hitting 100% coincides with the KR observation · blocked by N05–N08 (the skills under test) and N10 (the supervisor must point at the entry skill before a drain can exercise it)\n\n**Delegates to:** product-spike (experiment discipline — hypothesis, success metric, written finding).\n**On pickup:** run the experiment and write the finding (confirmed / falsified). Not a build node: honest outcomes are *confirmed* or *falsified*, not *shipped*.\n\n## What\n\nDrain 5 real issues of ordinary cycle work end-to-end through the new execution skills and grade KR1: how many reach Done with a merged PR, zero manual fix commits after the worker's final push, and the full review trail (verify verdict, What/Why/Focus PR body, review-summary comment). Write the finding.\n\n## Why\n\nKR1 is the stretch bet, and only live drains can grade it — D1's fixture scores prove the review gate, not the workflow; a skill that passes every dry run can still fail on a real issue's mess. Rejected alternative: declare victory on dry runs and toy issues — the exact unverified-claim failure this pack exists to prevent. `acceptance` because D2's Done is irreducible to its children: every skill can individually pass and the workflow still fail end-to-end.\n\n## Completion\n\n**Hypothesis:** a worker on first-party skills alone completes ≥4 of 5 real issues to Done + merged PR with zero post-push manual fix commits and the full review trail.\n\n**Success metric:** `drain-cycle grade` over `~/.drain-cycle/runs/*.json` + `git log` scan for post-push fix commits + Linear/PR trail check = **≥4/5**, measured over the first 5 issues drained after the skills land.\n\nBelow 4/5 **falsifies** the bet — D2 is re-shaped, not extended. Three consecutive drains needing manual fixes or third-party fallback fires the initiative **kill condition** (reinstall agent-skills, keep Shaper shaping-only, fold learnings into the README).\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- 5 issues of ordinary cycle work are available in the measurement window *(verified — the backlog convention keeps a cycle/ops stream; the KR's \"measured over\" clause anticipates this window)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** the 5 issues are too uniform (all markdown-pack work) and a 4/5 pass overstates generality. *Mitigation:* include at least one drain-cycle (Python) issue in the 5 so both repo types are exercised.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Drain the first validation issue end-to-end; record grade, post-push fix-commit count, and trail completeness in a trial note · Done when: the run log and trial note for issue 1 exist with all three measurements · Model: Fast · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] `acceptance` — Drain the remaining 4; evaluate the ≥4/5 success metric; write the finding (confirmed / falsified) — this finding is D2's Done condition · Done when: the finding is written with per-issue evidence links · Model: Balanced · axes H·M·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N09](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N09-validation-drains.md)"
}

the KR's \"measured over\" clause anticipates this window)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n* **Risk:** the 5 issues are too uniform (all markdown-pack work) and a 4/5 pass overstates generality. *Mitigation:* include at least one drain-cycle (Python) issue in the 5 so both repo types are exercised.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Drain the first validation issue end-to-end; {"id":"ABA-363","title":"N05 — Entry skill: the front door","description":"`story` · serves **KR1** · blocked by N04 (task breakdown waits for the accepted design doc)\n**Authoring strategy: NEW** — both predecessor packs are tracker-blind; nothing to port. superpowers' `subagent-driven-development` is the nearest relative for loop structure (reference, not port).\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); authoring per `docs/skill-anatomy.md` against the accepted N04 contract.\n\n## What\n\nAs a drain-cycle worker picking up a Linear issue, I want one front-door skill that takes me from pickup through breakdown-at-pickup, build, review, verify, and PR finishing, so that the supervisor prompt can be a single pointer and the whole procedure lives in the pack. This is the skill `drain_cycle/prompt.py` will point at (N10) — the keystone of the thin-supervisor architecture.\n\n## Why\n\nBreakdown-at-pickup on fresh context beats plan-time task expansion (detail decays before the node is reached), and one front door is what lets the supervisor prompt shrink to a pointer — the premise initiatives A and C share. Rejected alternative: a prompt-side checklist inside drain-cycle — workflow trapped in one vendor's supervisor, the exact coupling this initiative removes. Genuinely new authoring — this is the pack's structural edge over both predecessors. Unblocks N10.\n\n## Completion\n\n* **Done when:** the skill exists per `docs/skill-anatomy.md`, walks the N04 graph with every step a *named delegation* to its owning skill, and carries the issue's acceptance criteria through the handoff contract to the review step.\n* **Done when:** a dry run on one real issue reaches the PR step without re-prompting.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n* Linear issue context (body, AC, labels) is available at pickup *(verified — drain-cycle injects issue context into the worktree prompt today)*\n* The five-section node body is sufficient input for at-pickup breakdown *(to-verify — checked on the first validation drain)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n* **Risk:** the front door bloats into re-authored copies of the steps it orchestrates. *Mitigation:* P7 gate at review — every step a named delegation, no inlined procedure; \\~150-line execution-skill target makes inlining structurally impossible.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the front door end-to-end with each workflow step a named delegation to the build, debug/simplify, review (N03), verify, and PR skills (skill dir + frontmatter folded in) · Done when: a toy-issue dry run reaches the PR step with every step delegated by name · Model: Balanced · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = H·M·L·M·L\n- [ ] Write the breakdown-at-pickup section: size check + Done-when clause on every build task · Done when: breakdown of a sample node yields tasks each carrying exactly one verifiable Done-when clause · Model: Balanced · axes H·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Write the blocked/halt path per workflow governance: comment naming the blocker, issue stays In Progress, no false Done · Done when: dry run of a blocked issue ends with a Linear comment naming the blocker and unchanged status · Model: Fast · axes M·M·L·L·L\n\n---\n\nPlan {
  "id": "ABA-364",
  "description": "`story` · serves **KR1** · blocked by N04 (task breakdown waits for the accepted design doc)\n**Authoring strategy: PORT** — both packs ship `test-driven-development` (MIT); copy the stronger loop, modify only to add `[GATE]` markers, the verification-form fallback, and the per-slice commit convention.\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); authoring per `docs/skill-anatomy.md` against the accepted N04 contract.\n\n## What\n\nAs a worker building a broken-down task, I want a gated RED/GREEN/commit loop, so that every increment lands verified, smallest-first, with a commit trail a reviewer can replay. Per slice: a failing check first (RED), the minimal change that passes (GREEN), one commit — `[GATE]` markers non-optional.\n\n## Why\n\nThe gated TDD loop is the discipline both external packs converged on independently (superpowers' per-task implementer loop; agent-skills' /build) — convergent evolution is the strongest signal in the deep review, and exactly why this is a port, not a rewrite. Rejected alternative: advisory \"write tests first\" prose without gates — precisely what a worker under token pressure skips.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the skill enforces RED → GREEN → commit per slice, with `[GATE]` markers.\n- **Done when:** a verification-form fallback exists for repos with no test runner, chosen at breakdown time (gate script, grader, link check — a deterministic check, not necessarily a unit test).\n- **Done when:** a named escalation path into the debugging skill (N07) replaces retry-flailing after consecutive red loops.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Drained repos expose a runnable verification command discoverable from repo instructions *(to-verify — markdown-only repos like Shaper itself are the hard case; the fallback is the intended answer, checked on the first validation drain)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** in markdown-only repos RED/GREEN reads as meaningless and workers skip the skill wholesale. *Mitigation:* the verification-form fallback redefines RED as \"the deterministic check fails\" (e.g. `bin/check-plan-framing` non-zero); fallback selected at breakdown time, not improvised mid-build.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Port the RED/GREEN/commit loop core from the predecessor TDD skills (both packs, MIT), adding gates and the per-slice commit convention (skill dir + frontmatter folded in) · Done when: the ported skill passes anatomy section order and the loop's gates are marked `[GATE]` · Model: Balanced · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Write the verification-form fallback and the consecutive-failure escalation into the debugging skill · Done when: both paths are named delegations selectable at breakdown time · Model: Fast · axes M·M·L·L·L\n- [ ] Trial the loop on one toy task and record the transcript as the skill's worked example · Done when: transcript shows RED → GREEN → commit with no skipped gate · Model: Fast · axes L·L·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N06](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N06-build-skill-red-green-commit.md)"
}

{
  "id": "ABA-365",
  "description": "`story` · serves **KR1** · blocked by N04 (task breakdown waits for the accepted design doc)\n**Authoring strategy: PORT ×2** — superpowers' `systematic-debugging` + agent-skills' `code-simplification` (both MIT), light modification only (anatomy frontmatter, voice, N04 graph seams). Do not re-author proven discipline.\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); declare each skill's predecessor relation (port) in frontmatter.\n\n## What\n\nAs a worker stuck on a failing build or finishing a green one, I want systematic-debugging and simplification skills, so that failures resolve by hypothesis and evidence rather than retry-flailing, and green code sheds incidental complexity before review. The two domain skills confirmed at interview (frontend/perf/browser explicitly out).\n\n## Why\n\nThe two failure modes that most often force a human rescue mid-drain are undiagnosed failures (worker loops on retries) and over-built diffs (reviewer drowns) — these skills target exactly those. Rejected alternative: keep superpowers installed for its debugging skill alone — keeps the third-party dependency alive and makes KR3's uninstall impossible. Both are straight ports with light modification.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the debugging skill encodes hypothesis → instrument → bisect → fix with a written root-cause note as a gate (no fix without a stated cause).\n- **Done when:** the simplification skill runs as a post-green pass emitting a reviewable before/after rationale.\n- **Done when:** both are reachable by name from the build skill's escalation and exit points.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- Two skills (not one) is the right split — debugging fires mid-loop, simplification post-green *(verified — different trigger points in the N04 graph; folding would blur both triggers)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** the port mutates the source's proven discipline while adapting voice and anatomy — losing exactly the content that justified porting. *Mitigation:* frontmatter declares the predecessor relation (port); the PR notes what changed against the source and why, so review checks the deltas, not the whole text.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Port superpowers' `systematic-debugging` (MIT) with the root-cause-note gate added (skill dir + frontmatter folded in) · Done when: the ported skill passes anatomy order and the no-fix-without-stated-cause gate is marked `[GATE]` · Model: Fast · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·L·L·L·L\n- [ ] Port agent-skills' `code-simplification` (MIT) as the post-green pass with before/after rationale · Done when: the ported skill emits a reviewable simplification note on a sample diff · Model: Fast · axes M·L·L·L·L\n- [ ] Wire both into the build skill's escalation and exit points by name · Done when: the build skill names both delegations and neither is inlined · Model: Fast · axes L·L·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N07](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N07-debugging-and-simplification.md)"
}

{
  "id": "ABA-366",
  "description": "`story` · serves **KR1** · blocked by N04 (task breakdown waits for the accepted design doc) · consumes N03's review-summary\n**Authoring strategy: HYBRID** — superpowers' `finishing-a-development-branch` (MIT) is the skeleton (verify-then-finish flow ports straight across); the Graphite path, What/Why/Focus body, and Linear trail steps are the new parts.\n\n**Delegates to:** at-pickup task breakdown (story); verify the gt command surface against current Graphite docs before relying on it (HS companion: source-driven-development).\n\n## What\n\nAs a worker with a verified diff, I want a Graphite-first PR finishing skill with a plain-git fallback, so that every drain ends in a stacked, reviewable PR carrying a What/Why/Focus body and a review-summary comment instead of an unreviewed push. The trail artefacts this skill emits are exactly what KR1's \"full review trail\" check greps for.\n\n## Why\n\nGraphite-first matches the owner's tooling and drain-cycle's half-built stack mode (`.drain-handoff.json`), so stacking works where it matters without stranding environments that lack `gt`. Rejected alternatives, both directions: plain-git-only (abandons stacking) and Graphite-only (breaks any repo or worker without gt). Per-repo push policy stays with repo instructions; the skill honours it.\n\n## Completion\n\n- **Done when:** the skill detects `gt` and submits a stacked PR; when absent, the plain-git path produces a branch + PR with the identical body/trail contract.\n- **Done when:** every finish lands the What/Why/Focus PR body and posts the review-summary comment to the Linear issue.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- The gt command surface used (branch create / submit) is stable across worker environments *(to-verify — pin the verified command set during authoring; source-driven-development companion fires on the skeleton task)*\n- Per-repo push policy is readable from repo instructions *(verified — this repo's AGENTS.md states it)*\n\n## Key Risks\n\n- **Risk:** Graphite and git paths drift — different bodies or trail artefacts — making KR1's trail check flaky depending on path. *Mitigation:* one shared body/trail template both paths fill; the fallback task's Done-when asserts artefact parity.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- [ ] `skeleton` — Author the Graphite-first flow (gt detection → branch → stacked submit) on the ported finishing-a-development-branch skeleton, with the What/Why/Focus body template (skill dir + shared trail template folded in) · Done when: a toy diff lands as a stacked PR with the body contract filled · Model: Balanced · review elevated · axes RC·SC·HS·SR·OR = M·M·H·M·L · companions source-driven-development\n- [ ] Write the plain-git fallback with trail parity · Done when: the same toy diff finished via the fallback yields identical body and trail artefacts · Model: Fast · axes M·M·M·L·L\n- [ ] Write the review-summary comment + Linear status update step · Done when: the issue shows the review-summary comment and status moves per governance at the moment of state change · Model: Fast · axes L·L·L·L·L\n\n---\nPlan source: [N08](https://github.com/ababushkin/agent-skills-shaper/blob/main/examples/delivery-plans/issues-drain-end-to-end/D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/N08-pr-finishing-graphite-first.md)"
}

It's **not a skill** — it's the benchmark workspace left over from developing the `plan-review` skill, sitting inside `skills/` without a `SKILL.md`. Five iteration directories, each holding an eval run of plan-review against 5 scenarios: `benchmark.json`/`benchmark.md` (results), `grader-prompt.md`, `feedback.json`, and an `aggregate.py`. The iteration-1 run from May shows what it was for — measuring the skill's lift (87% pass with skill vs 44% without, at +11k tokens).

Two things follow from that:

1. **My count last answer was off by one** — the pack has **14 skills** today, so post-initiative-A the peak is **20 skills**, not 21. The plugin loader skips this directory anyway (no `SKILL.md`), so nothing functional changes.
2. This workspace is load-bearing for **initiative B**: its KR2 ("plan-review 5-scenario benchmark ≥90% post-reform, baseline 93%") is measured with exactly this harness — the consolidation can't prove it didn't degrade plan-review without it.

It is arguably misfiled, though — working data living under `skills/` where only skill directories belong. A natural home would be `examples/` or a top-level `benchmarks/`, and initiative B (which already touches the directory layout) is the obvious moment to move it. Want me to relocate it now instead, or leave it for B?

1	# Delivery plan — Issues drain end-to-end on first-party skills
2	
3	The delivery hierarchy for initiative A of the lifecycle expansion, emitted by `delivery-shape`
4	per [`docs/delivery-shape-contract.md`](../../../docs/delivery-shape-contract.md).
5	
6	**Source initiative:** [Issues drain end-to-end on first-party
7	skills](https://linear.app/ababushkin/project/issues-drain-end-to-end-on-first-party-skills-be562671c8d8)
8	· Linear `ABA` · Type 1 (methodology skill pack) · dominant model tier Balanced. Source package:
9	[`docs/ideas/lifecycle-expansion.md`](../../../docs/ideas/lifecycle-expansion.md) §4.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## The bet (read this first — top-down starts at the outcome)
14	
15	**Goal:** For drain-cycle workers (and Anton driving interactively), make every picked-up Linear
16	issue flow from pickup to a merged, reviewable PR on Shaper skills alone — review trail attached,
17	no rescue by a human and no reliance on third-party packs.
18	
19	| KR | Claim | Role | Served by |
20	|----|-------|------|-----------|
21	| **KR1** *(stretch)* | ≥4 of the next 5 drained issues reach Done with a merged PR and zero manual fix commits after the worker's final push, with the full review trail present (verify verdict, What/Why/Focus PR body, review-summary comment). | bet | **D2** |
22	| **KR2** *(commit)* | The review/verify skills surface ≥9 of 10 seeded Critical/Required findings when run against fixture diffs with known defects, via `bin/grade-execution-review fixtures/execution-review/`. | foundation | **D1** |
23	| **KR3** *(commit)* | 100% of drained issues in the window invoke the new execution skills and zero invoke superpowers/agent-skills; both packs uninstalled and zero references to their skill names remain in the Shaper repo or drain-cycle prompts. | brake | **D3** |
24	
25	**Appetite:** ~10 issues. This plan emits **11 nodes** — one over, carried by D3's two
26	deliberately thin cutover nodes (different repos, so they don't merge). Flagged here rather than
27	silently absorbed; if the cycle squeezes, N11's audit task folds into N09's acceptance task.
28	
29	**Kill condition:** If, after the execution skills ship, 3 consecutive drained issues require
30	manual fix commits or fall back to third-party pack skills, stop — reinstall agent-skills, keep
31	Shaper shaping-only, and fold the learnings into the pack's README.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## How to read this plan top-down
36	
37	Three layers, each mapping to one tracker artefact. Read outward from the bet above:
38	
39	```
40	initiative (this README)            ← goal + KRs
41	└── deliverable  D*/_deliverable.md  → milestone   (tagged serves_kr)
42	    └── node  N*.md                   → issue        (polymorphic: story/adr/design-doc/experiment/…)
43	        └── task  - [ ] in node        → sub-issue    (`skeleton` task opens the path; `acceptance` task closes it)
44	```
45	
46	Directory nesting **is** the hierarchy; numeric `D*/N*` prefixes give deterministic ordering.
47	Default working order is D1 → D2 → D3, with two cross-deliverable dependencies named as
48	`> **Blocked by:**` callouts in the dependent nodes: N09's validation drains need N10's prompt
49	pointer in place first, and N11's audit reads N09's transcripts.
50	
51	## Tree
52	
53	```
54	issues-drain-end-to-end/
55	├── README.md                                          ← you are here (initiative root)
56	├── D1-review-gate-proven-on-seeded-defects/           → milestone · serves KR2
57	│   ├── _deliverable.md
58	│   ├── N01 … fixture corpus + review grader              · story · skeleton
59	│   ├── N02 … ADR: persona contract + dispatch protocol   · adr
60	│   └── N03 … personas + review fan-out skill             · story
61	├── D2-execution-workflow-drains-issues/               → milestone · serves KR1
62	│   ├── _deliverable.md
63	│   ├── N04 … execution-workflow design doc (Rule A1)     · design-doc
64	│   ├── N05 … entry skill — the front door                · story
65	│   ├── N06 … build skill — RED/GREEN/commit loop         · story
66	│   ├── N07 … debugging + simplification skills           · story
67	│   ├── N08 … PR finishing — Graphite-first, git fallback · story
68	│   └── N09 … validation drains (5 issues, ≥4/5)          · experiment · [acceptance]
69	└── D3-cutover-off-third-party-packs/                  → milestone · serves KR3
70	    ├── _deliverable.md
71	    ├── N10 … drain-cycle prompt pointer                  · story
72	    └── N11 … uninstall both packs + purge references     · story
73	```
74	
75	## Node-type coverage
76	
77	| Type | Completion-criterion form | Exercised by |
78	|------|---------------------------|--------------|
79	| `story` | acceptance criteria (Cohn form) | N01, N03, N05, N06, N07, N08, N10, N11 |
80	| `adr` | accepted decision record | N02 |
81	| `design-doc` | the accepted design doc (Rule A1 branch) | N04 |
82	| `experiment` | hypothesis + success metric | N09 |
83	
84	This is the first plan to exercise the `design-doc` type on real work (the Rule A1 branch was
85	previously grounded only by the `_tests/rule-a1-branch/` fixture).
86	
87	**Flags** (orthogonal to type): **N01** carries `skeleton: true` — the initiative's walking
88	skeleton proves the fixture → persona-run → grade seam end-to-end before any real persona exists.
89	**N09** carries `acceptance: true` (verifies D2) — D2's Done is irreducible to ∀child.done:
90	every skill can individually pass and the workflow still fail end-to-end, so the live-drain
91	experiment closes the deliverable. Close it last.

I've reviewed all 11 issues (ABA-359 through ABA-369) against the plan files and the repo's shared files. Here's the slicing, grounded in what each issue actually touches.

## The stacks

**Stack 1 — D1 review gate (3 PRs, Shaper repo)**

| PR | Issue | Footprint |
|----|-------|-----------|
| 1.1 | ABA-359 N01 fixtures + grader | `fixtures/execution-review/`, `bin/grade-execution-review` |
| 1.2 | ABA-360 N02 persona ADR | one new ADR doc |
| 1.3 | ABA-362 N03 personas + fan-out skill | persona files, `skills/<review>/SKILL.md`, command wrapper |

Stacked rather than parallel because the grader's finding-line format (1.1) and the ADR that pins it (1.2) must agree, and N03 is blocked by N02 anyway. Each PR is a few hundred lines of markdown plus one script — comfortably reviewable.

**Stack 2 — ABA-361 N04 design doc (1 PR, parallel with Stack 1)**

Single PR, one new doc. Its file footprint is disjoint from Stack 1, so it can be in review concurrently with zero conflict risk. One content caveat: N04 will cite N02's contract, so merge PR 1.2 before finalising N04's review (or have N04 cite the ADR by ID and tolerate concurrent review).

**Stack 3 — D2 skills (4 PRs, based on main after N04 merges)**

| PR | Issue | Footprint |
|----|-------|-----------|
| 3.1 | ABA-364 N06 build skill | `skills/<build>/`, wrapper |
| 3.2 | ABA-365 N07 debug + simplify | two skill dirs, wrappers, **plus edits to N06's skill file** |
| 3.3 | ABA-366 N08 PR finishing | `skills/<pr-finish>/`, shared trail template in `references/` |
| 3.4 | ABA-363 N05 entry skill | `skills/<entry>/`, wrapper, **all README table rows for the stack** |

N05 goes on top deliberately: it names every other skill as a delegation, so reviewing it only makes sense once the targets exist below it in the stack.

**Tail — sequential singles, not a stack**

- ABA-367 N10: drain-cycle repo — different repo entirely, so it's its own one-PR change with no conflict surface against Shaper. Needs N05 merged first (the skill name it points at).
- ABA-368 N09: the validation-drain finding write-up + plan checkbox ticks. Small PR after the drains run.
- ABA-369 N11: uninstall + purge. Last by construction (blocked by N03 + N09), and by then everything else has merged.

## Where conflicts will happen, and the cheap avoidance

**1. README.md — the real hotspot.** Up to six PRs want to touch it: N03 and N05–N08 each add skill-table rows, and N11 rewrites the "execution is delegated to an execution pack of your choice" framing. Adjacent-row insertions in the same table are the classic restack conflict — when PR 3.1 absorbs review feedback, `gt restack` re-applies 3.2–3.4 and trips on the table every time.
*Avoidance:* skill PRs add only their own `skills/<name>/` dir and wrapper; all README rows land in the **top PR of each stack** (1.3 and 3.4). One rule, no tooling. N11's framing rewrite happens after everything merged, so it's free.

**2. N07 edits N06's file — guaranteed conflict if parallelised.** N07's third task ("wire both into the build skill's escalation and exit points") modifies the build skill that PR 3.1 creates. If a drain worker authored N06 and N07 in parallel worktrees off main, this collides every time.
*Avoidance:* stack 3.2 directly on 3.1 — this is exactly what Graphite exists for. Don't move the wiring task into N05's PR to enable parallelism; that's the overcomplication you said to skip.

**3. Cross-stack name drift — content breakage, not a git conflict.** N05 and N08 reference Stack 1's review skill and review-summary format by name. If Stack 1's review renames something while Stack 3 is in flight, git won't complain — the delegation just silently dangles.
*Avoidance:* already structurally handled — N02 (ADR) and N04 (design doc) pin the names and contracts and are review-gated *before* any D2 build starts. The only discipline needed is honouring the existing blocked-by edges: don't start Stack 3 authoring until N04 is accepted.

**4. Non-issues, verified:** `plugin.json` doesn't enumerate skills (the loader auto-discovers `skills/*/SKILL.md`), so skill PRs don't touch it. Command wrappers are one file per skill — disjoint. Each issue ticks checkboxes only in its own `N*.md` plan file — disjoint.

## Merge order

Stack 1 ∥ Stack 2 → Stack 3 → N10 (drain-cycle) → N09 → N11. Ten PRs across two repos, 1:1 with issues (which matches drain-cycle's one-worker-per-issue model), deepest stack is four small markdown PRs.

One footnote: this repo's standing convention is push-direct-to-main with PRs only on request — running initiative A through Graphite stacks is a deviation you'd be opting into (and a nice dogfood of N08's own skill). If you want, I can record this slicing as comments on the Linear issues so drain workers see their stack position at pickup.

1	"""Prompt builder for spawned ``claude -p`` sessions.
2	
3	The prompt is the entire contract between the orchestrator and the spawned
4	agent — there's no system prompt, no multi-turn loop. The four-segment
5	ordering below is load-bearing: the agent reads top-down, so context
6	(title + body) comes before instructions (preamble + tail), and the tail
7	line is last so it stays in the trailing-tokens window the model attends
8	to most strongly.
9	"""
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	from pathlib import Path
13	from typing import Any
14	
15	_VERIFY_FLOW_LABEL = "verify"
16	
17	
18	def is_verify_flow(issue: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
19	    """Return True when the issue carries the ``verify`` label."""
20	    return _VERIFY_FLOW_LABEL in issue.get("labels", [])
21	
22	
23	def _shape_task_directive(identifier: str) -> str:
24	    """Shape-task preamble for verify-flow worker sessions.
25	
26	    Instructs the worker to check for an existing Task Shaper output
27	    block in the Linear issue body before invoking ``/shape:task``. The
28	    check-first approach handles both fresh sessions (block absent →
29	    invoke) and §14 resumes (block present → reuse).
30	    """
31	    return (
32	        f"Shaping step (run before implementing): fetch the Linear issue body "
33	        f"for {identifier} and check for a Task Shaper output block "
34	        "(delimited by `<!-- TASK-SHAPER-START -->` and `<!-- TASK-SHAPER-END -->`). "
35	        "If the block is present, use it as your implementation guide and skip "
36	        "re-running `/shape:task`. If the block is absent, run "
37	        f"`/shape:task {identifier}` first and use its output as your "
38	        "implementation guide.\n\n"
39	    )
40	
41	
42	_TAIL = (
43	    "before marking Done: run /code-review-and-quality on the working-tree "
44	    "changes, fix Critical/Required findings, commit + push, then post a "
45	    "review-summary comment on the issue and transition to Done."
46	)
47	
48	_STACK_TAIL = (
49	    "before marking Done: run /code-review-and-quality on the working-tree "
50	    "changes, fix Critical/Required findings, commit to the issue branch "
51	    "without pushing, write .drain-handoff.json, then post a review-summary "
52	    "comment on the issue and transition to Done."
53	)
54	
55	
56	def _resume_directive(identifier: str) -> str:
57	    """Resume preamble for a worktree carrying prior committed work.
58	
59	    Inserted as the first line inside the preamble (after the ``---``
60	    separator, before "Execution instructions:") so the agent reads it
61	    ahead of the procedure but the tail still holds the last-line
62	    position the four-segment ordering reserves for it.
63	    """
64	    return (
65	        f"Resuming issue {identifier}: this worktree carries prior committed "
66	        "work from an earlier session that was halted. Run "
67	        "`git log --oneline main..HEAD` and `git status` first to read what "
68	        "is already done, then continue from that point — do not restart "
69	        "from scratch.\n\n"
70	    )
71	
72	
73	def _normal_preamble(
74	    identifier: str, worktree: Path, resume_segment: str, shape_task_segment: str
75	) -> str:
76	    return (
77	        "---\n\n"
78	        f"{resume_segment}"
79	        f"{shape_task_segment}"
80	        "Execution instructions:\n"
81	        f"- Working directory: {worktree}\n"
82	        "- Base branch: main\n"
83	        f"- Completion sequence for issue {identifier} (run in this order, "
84	        "before marking Done):\n"
85	        "  1. Run `/code-review-and-quality` against the working-tree changes.\n"
86	        "  2. Fix any Critical or Required findings. Lower-severity findings "
87	        "are at your discretion.\n"
88	        "  3. Commit and push to main.\n"
89	        "  4. Post a short review-summary comment on the Linear issue via "
90	        "`mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_comment` (count of findings by severity, "
91	        "fixed vs deferred).\n"
92	        "  5. Transition issue to Done via `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue` "
93	        '(state: "Done").\n'
94	    )
95	
96	
97	def _stack_preamble(
98	    identifier: str, worktree: Path, resume_segment: str, shape_task_segment: str
99	) -> str:
100	    return (
101	        "---\n\n"
102	        f"{resume_segment}"
103	        f"{shape_task_segment}"
104	        "Execution instructions:\n"
105	        f"- Working directory: {worktree}\n"
106	        "- Base branch: main\n"
107	        f"- Completion sequence for issue {identifier} (run in this order, "
108	        "before marking Done):\n"
109	        "  1. Run `/code-review-and-quality` against the working-tree changes.\n"
110	        "  2. Fix any Critical or Required findings. Lower-severity findings "
111	        "are at your discretion.\n"
112	        "  3. Commit to the issue branch (do not push).\n"
113	        "  4. Write `.drain-handoff.json` in the worktree root with keys:\n"
114	        "     - `pr_title`: a concise PR title (≤ 70 characters)\n"
115	        "     - `pr_body`: markdown with ## What, ## Why, and ## What to review "
116	        "sections\n"
117	        '     - `findings`: `{"critical": N, "required": N}` counts from the '
118	        "review\n"
119	        "  5. Post a short review-summary comment on the Linear issue via "
120	        "`mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_comment` (count of findings by severity, "
121	        "fixed vs deferred).\n"
122	        "  6. Transition issue to Done via `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue` "
123	        '(state: "Done").\n'
124	    )
125	
126	
127	def build(
128	    issue: dict[str, Any],
129	    worktree: Path,
130	    *,
131	    resumed: bool = False,
132	    stack: bool = False,
133	) -> str:
134	    title = issue.get("title", "")
135	    description = issue.get("description") or ""
136	    identifier = issue.get("identifier", "")
137	
138	    resume_segment = _resume_directive(identifier) if resumed else ""
139	    shape_task_segment = _shape_task_directive(identifier) if is_verify_flow(issue) else ""
140	
141	    if stack:
142	        preamble = _stack_preamble(identifier, worktree, resume_segment, shape_task_segment)
143	        tail = _STACK_TAIL
144	    else:
145	        preamble = _normal_preamble(identifier, worktree, resume_segment, shape_task_segment)
146	        tail = _TAIL
147	
148	    return (
149	        f"# {title}\n\n"
150	        f"{description}\n\n"
151	        f"{preamble}\n"
152	        f"{tail}\n"
153	    )

16	
17	@dataclass(frozen=True)
18	class HandoffData:
19	    pr_title: str
20	    pr_body: str
21	    findings: dict[str, int]
22	
23	
24	def write(worktree: Path, data: HandoffData) -> None:
25	    """Serialise ``data`` to ``<worktree>/.drain-handoff.json``."""
26	    path = worktree / HANDOFF_FILE
27	    path.write_text(
28	        json.dumps(
29	            {
30	                "pr_title": data.pr_title,
31	                "pr_body": data.pr_body,
32	                "findings": data.findings,
33	            },
34	            indent=2,
35	        )
36	    )
37	
38	
39	def read(worktree: Path) -> HandoffData | None:
40	    """Return the handoff data for ``worktree``, or ``None`` if absent or invalid."""
41	    path = worktree / HANDOFF_FILE
42	    try:
43	        payload = json.loads(path.read_text())
44	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
45	        return None
46	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
47	        return None
48	    pr_title = payload.get("pr_title")
49	    pr_body = payload.get("pr_body")
50	    findings = payload.get("findings")
51	    if not isinstance(pr_title, str) or not isinstance(pr_body, str):
52	        return None
53	    if not isinstance(findings, dict):
54	        return None
55	    return HandoffData(pr_title=pr_title, pr_body=pr_body, findings=findings)
56

/Users/anton/src/drain-cycle/docs/design-decisions.md:94:**Why `start_new_session=True` + `os.killpg`.** The old `subprocess.run(timeout=)` killed only the direct child on timeout, orphaning grandchildren — MCP servers, sub-agents — that kept consuming. Making the worker a process-group leader and SIGKILLing the whole group on the time cap reaps them. SIGKILL with no SIGTERM grace is deliberate: a session past its deadline has no clean-shutdown work worth waiting for, and SIGKILL is the only signal a wedged grandchild cannot ignore. Killing the group also closes the stdout pipe those grandchildren inherited, which is what lets the reader thread reach EOF instead of blocking.

1	"""``drain-cycle`` CLI entry point.
2	
3	Zero-arg invocation drains the current Linear cycle. Each issue's target
4	repo is resolved from a ``repo:<name>`` label against
5	``~/.drain-cycle/repos.yml``; the operator runs ``drain-cycle`` from
6	anywhere, not from inside a target repo. The ``grade`` subcommand reads
7	the run logs and prints a health read.
8	
9	Secrets load before any module reads ``os.environ``, first hit wins:
10	shell-exported vars → ``~/.drain-cycle/.env`` → the drain-cycle repo
11	root ``.env`` (dev-checkout fallback, absent once installed as a uv
12	tool). ``load_dotenv`` defaults to ``override=False``, so an
13	already-set var always beats a later source and the shell always wins.
14	
15	``repos.yml`` and the optional ``limits.yml`` are validated eagerly at
16	startup so a broken config halts exit 1 on stderr before any Linear
17	traffic or run-log file is written — there is no cycle yet to log
18	against. ``limits.yml`` is optional (its absence yields the baked-in
19	guardrail defaults); a present-but-malformed one still halts.
20	"""
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import sys
24	from pathlib import Path
25	
26	from dotenv import load_dotenv
27	
28	from . import grade, grade_draft, limits, orchestrator, repos, telemetry
29	
30	_REPO_ENV = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".env"
31	
32	
33	def _load_secrets() -> None:
34	    """Populate ``os.environ`` from the first ``.env`` that defines each key.
35	
36	    ``~/.drain-cycle/.env`` sits beside ``repos.yml`` and the run logs,
37	    so an installed tool finds its secret there. The repo-root ``.env``
38	    is a dev-checkout fallback only — once installed as a uv tool the
39	    package lives in an isolated env where that path has no ``.env``.
40	    ``$HOME`` is resolved per call so tests can redirect it.
41	    """
42	    load_dotenv(Path.home() / ".drain-cycle" / ".env")
43	    load_dotenv(_REPO_ENV)
44	
45	
46	_USAGE = (
47	    "usage: drain-cycle [--watch|-w]       drain the current Linear cycle\n"
48	    "       drain-cycle grade              print health read from run logs\n"
49	    "       drain-cycle grade-draft <issue> write per-ticket grade draft\n"
50	    "       drain-cycle status             show status of the active run\n"
51	    "       drain-cycle --help\n"
52	    "\n"
53	    "options:\n"
54	    "  --watch, -w   open a tmux split-pane per issue running the live\n"
55	    "                claude session (requires running inside tmux)"
56	)
57	
58	_WATCH_FLAGS = frozenset(["--watch", "-w"])
59	
60	
61	def main() -> None:
62	    import os
63	
64	    _load_secrets()
65	    # Telemetry reads its key from the environment just populated above; a
66	    # no-op when HONEYCOMB_API_KEY is unset, so an unconfigured run is
67	    # unchanged. Registers its own atexit flush, hence no teardown here.
68	    telemetry.setup()
69	    argv = sys.argv[1:]
70	
71	    # Drain invocation: zero or more flags, no subcommand.
72	    # Currently only --watch/-w is recognised.
73	    remaining = [a for a in argv if a not in _WATCH_FLAGS]
74	    watch = any(a in _WATCH_FLAGS for a in argv)
75	
76	    if not remaining:
77	        if watch and not os.environ.get("TMUX"):
78	            print(
79	                "drain-cycle: --watch ignored: $TMUX not set — run inside tmux to "
80	                "watch the live session; falling back to normal execution",
81	                file=sys.stderr,
82	            )
83	        try:
84	            loaded_repos = repos.load()
85	            loaded_limits = limits.load()
86	        except (repos.RepoConfigError, limits.LimitsConfigError) as exc:
87	            print(f"drain-cycle: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
88	            sys.exit(1)
89	        sys.exit(orchestrator.run(loaded_repos, loaded_limits, watch=watch))
90	
91	    if remaining == ["grade"] and not watch:
92	        sys.exit(grade.run(grade.default_runs_dir()))
93	    if (
94	        len(remaining) == 2
95	        and remaining[0] == "grade-draft"
96	        and not watch
97	    ):
98	        sys.exit(grade_draft.run(remaining[1]))
99	    if remaining == ["status"] and not watch:
100	        from . import status
101	        sys.exit(status.run())
102	    if argv in (["-h"], ["--help"]):
103	        print(_USAGE)
104	        sys.exit(0)
105	    print(f"drain-cycle: unknown invocation: {' '.join(argv)}", file=sys.stderr)
106	    print(_USAGE, file=sys.stderr)
107	    sys.exit(2)
108

"""Graphite + GitHub CLI primitives for assembling a per-repo PR stack.

Commands run from the per-issue worktree root (``cwd=worktree``), where ``gt``
reads the shared ``.git/.graphite_metadata.db``. Telemetry spans mirror
``worktree.py``: ``drain.graphite.*`` span names, capture-stderr →
``RuntimeError`` pattern.

Per-repo preconditions (one-time, operator-owned, not automatable under
``--dangerously-skip-permissions``):

  gt auth             # interactive browser flow
  gt init --trunk main

If either is absent, ``gt submit`` aborts before any push and the
``RuntimeError`` propagates to the orchestrator's stop-the-line halt.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from . import telemetry

_REVIEW_HIGH_COLOR = "B60205"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PrInfo:
    url: str
    number: int


def submit(worktree: Path, *, parent: str, body: str = "") -> PrInfo:
    """Track the branch in Graphite and submit the full stack.

    Runs ``gt track --parent <parent>``, ``gt submit --stack
    --no-interactive --publish``, then fetches the current branch's PR
    info via ``gh pr view``. Raises ``RuntimeError`` (capturing stderr)
    on any non-zero exit — callers treat this as a stop-the-line halt.
    """
    with telemetry.tracer.start_as_current_span("drain.graphite.submit") as span:
        span.set_attribute("graphite.parent", parent)
        span.set_attribute("graphite.worktree", str(worktree))
        _run(["gt", "track", "--parent", parent], cwd=worktree)
        _run(["gt", "submit", "--stack", "--no-interactive", "--publish"], cwd=worktree)
        raw = _run_output(["gh", "pr", "view", "--json", "number,url"], cwd=worktree)
        try:
            data = json.loads(raw)
            info = PrInfo(url=data["url"], number=data["number"])
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError) as exc:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"gh pr view returned unexpected output: {exc!r}"
            ) from exc
        if body:
            _run(["gh", "pr", "edit", str(info.number), "--body", body], cwd=worktree)
        span.set_attribute("graphite.pr_number", info.number)
        span.set_attribute("graphite.pr_url", info.url)
        return info


def ensure_review_high_label(worktree: Path) -> None:
    """Create the ``review:high`` GitHub label if absent (idempotent via ``--force``)."""
    with telemetry.tracer.start_as_current_span("drain.graphite.ensure_label"):
        _run(
            ["gh", "label", "create", "review:high",
             "--color", _REVIEW_HIGH_COLOR, "--force"],
            cwd=worktree,
        )


def add_label(pr_number: int, label: str, worktree: Path) -> None:
    """Add a label to the specified GitHub PR."""
    with telemetry.tracer.start_as_current_span("drain.graphite.add_label") as span:
        span.set_attribute("graphite.pr_number", pr_number)
        span.set_attribute("graphite.label", label)
        _run(["gh", "pr", "edit", str(pr_number), "--add-label", label], cwd=worktree)


def _run(args: list[str], *, cwd: Path) -> None:
    result = subprocess.run(
        args,
        cwd=cwd,
        check=False,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{' '.join(args)} failed (exit {result.returncode}): "
            f"{result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip() or '<no output>'}"
        )


def _run_output(args: list[str], *, cwd: Path) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(
        args,
        cwd=cwd,
        check=False,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{' '.join(args)} failed (exit {result.returncode}): "
            f"{result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip() or '<no output>'}"
        )
    return result.stdout

  +   - **Direct mode** (interactive session, not spawned by drain-cycle): commit the reviewed version and push to main. This repo pushes directly to main; PRs only when the owner asks. An issue isn't Done if work only exists locally.
  +   - **Drain mode** (spawned by the drain-cycle orchestrator in a worktree): commit and submit a PR via `gt submit --stack --no-interactive --publish`. The orchestrator automatically posts the PR link back to the Linear issue after the worker exits and the issue is confirmed Done — the agent does not need to post the PR link itself.
  +4. **Summary comment** — Post a short comment on the Linear issue via `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_comment` with the review summary (count of findings by severity, plus what was fixed vs deferred).    5. **Done** — Transition to Done via `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue`.
   
   Status updates happen at the moment of state change — not batched at end of session.

  +### PR links
  +
  +When a spawned agent creates a PR (via `gt submit`), the orchestrator finds it after the issue is confirmed Done and:
  +
  +- Records `pr_url`, `pr_number`, `review_high`, and `parent_branch` in the run-log entry.
  +- Posts a comment on the Linear issue with the PR link (and a `review:high` flag if the PR carries that label).
  +
  +This lookup uses the `gh` CLI and the branch name (the issue identifier) to find the PR. If `gh` is unavailable or no PR exists for that branch, the fields are `null` and no comment is posted — the drain continues normally either way. See [`docs/design-decisions.md`](docs/design-decisions.md) §17.
  +
   ### Debug capture
   
   Workers spawn in an isolated worktree. drain-cycle symlinks the repo's project-scoped config (`.claude/`, `.mcp.json`, and any extra paths you configure — see Install) into each worktree, so a worker loads the same settings, hooks, agents, and skills as an interactive session at the repo root, including project-scoped hooks like entire.io's checkpointing. [`docs/design-decisions.md`](docs/design-decisions.md) §10 documents the mechanism.

Your requirement was that drain-cycle auto-creates PRs when it executes the initiative-A issues. Verified against the code, it currently won't:

- But only ABA-301's half ever reached main. The other three commits are stranded on local branches in `~/src/drain-cycle` (`661b5c6`, `e6275c9`, `35e7053`), never pushed, never merged. That violates drain-cycle's own AGENTS.md rule ("an issue isn't Done if work only exists locally") — and worse, the three branches were authored in parallel and **disagree with each other**: ABA-302 has the orchestrator submit the PR from the handoff file; ABA-303/304 assume the *worker* runs `gt submit` itself and the orchestrator merely looks the PR up afterwards. ABA-302 was even written against a different handoff filename/schema than the one that actually merged.

So the blocker for your requirement is precisely these unmerged, mutually inconsistent branches.

34	
35	def submit(worktree: Path, *, parent: str, body: str = "") -> PrInfo:
36	    """Track the branch in Graphite and submit the full stack.
37	
38	    Runs ``gt track --parent <parent>``, ``gt submit --stack
39	    --no-interactive --publish``, then fetches the current branch's PR
40	    info via ``gh pr view``. Raises ``RuntimeError`` (capturing stderr)
41	    on any non-zero exit — callers treat this as a stop-the-line halt.
42	    """
43	    with telemetry.tracer.start_as_current_span("drain.graphite.submit") as span:
44	        span.set_attribute("graphite.parent", parent)
45	        span.set_attribute("graphite.worktree", str(worktree))
46	        _run(["gt", "track", "--parent", parent], cwd=worktree)
47	        _run(["gt", "submit", "--stack", "--no-interactive", "--publish"], cwd=worktree)
48	        raw = _run_output(["gh", "pr", "view", "--json", "number,url"], cwd=worktree)
49	        try:
50	            data = json.loads(raw)
51	            info = PrInfo(url=data["url"], number=data["number"])
52	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError) as exc:
53	            raise RuntimeError(
54	                f"gh pr view returned unexpected output: {exc!r}"
55	            ) from exc
56	        if body:
57	            _run(["gh", "pr", "edit", str(info.number), "--body", body], cwd=worktree)
58	        span.set_attribute("graphite.pr_number", info.number)
59	        span.set_attribute("graphite.pr_url", info.url)
60	        return info

225	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
226	# Test 3: gt submit failure → halt + run-log + worktree preserved
227	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
228	
229	def test_graphite_failure_halts_cycle_and_preserves_worktree(
230	    tmp_path: Path,
231	    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
232	    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
233	) -> None:
234	    """A simulated gt submit failure must halt the cycle, record the failure
235	    in the run-log (with the issue's Done final state), and leave the worktree
236	    on disk for recovery. The second issue must never be attempted."""
237	    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
238	    repo.mkdir()
239	    _init_repo(repo)
240	    monkeypatch.chdir(repo)
241	    monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(tmp_path))
242	
243	    first = _issue("ABA-FIRST", sort_order=1.0)
244	    second = _issue("ABA-SECOND", sort_order=2.0)
245	    done_marker = tmp_path / "done.txt"
246	
247	    _wire_linear_stubs([first, second], done_marker, monkeypatch)
248	    monkeypatch.setattr(
249	        orchestrator, "_CLAUDE_CMD", [str(_write_done_claude_script(tmp_path, done_marker))]
250	    )
251	    monkeypatch.setattr(handoff, "read", lambda path: handoff.Findings())
252	
253	    graphite_error = "gt submit failed: auth token missing"
254	
255	    def failing_submit(worktree: Path, *, parent: str, body: str = "") -> graphite.PrInfo:
256	        raise RuntimeError(graphite_error)
257	
258	    monkeypatch.setattr(graphite, "submit", failing_submit)
259	
260	    exit_code = orchestrator.run(_stub_repos(repo))
261	
262	    assert exit_code == 1
263	
264	    # Worktree for the first issue preserved (not removed on graphite halt).
265	    first_worktree = repo / ".worktrees" / first["identifier"]
266	    assert first_worktree.is_dir()
267	
268	    # Second issue never attempted (cycle halted after first).
269	    second_worktree = repo / ".worktrees" / second["identifier"]
270	    assert not second_worktree.exists()
271	
272	    # Run-log records the failure.
273	    runs_dir = tmp_path / ".drain-cycle" / "runs"
274	    log_files = list(runs_dir.glob("stub-cycle-*.json"))
275	    assert len(log_files) == 1
276	    payload = json.loads(log_files[0].read_text())
277	    assert len(payload["entries"]) == 1
278	    entry = payload["entries"][0]
279	    assert entry["issue_identifier"] == first["identifier"]
280	    # Issue reached Done in Linear; the halt is at the orchestrator/stack layer.
281	    assert entry["final_linear_state"] == "Done"
282	    assert entry["halt_reason"] is not None
283	    assert graphite_error in entry["halt_reason"]
284	
285	    # Halt line on stderr carries the error detail.
286	    stderr_lines = capsys.readouterr().err.splitlines()
287	    halt_lines = [line for line in stderr_lines if line.startswith("Halt: ")]
288	    assert len(halt_lines) == 1
289	    assert graphite_error in halt_lines[0]
290

"""Root conftest.py for the ABA-302 worktree.

The editable install points to the main-branch source tree. When pytest runs
from this worktree, that installed copy shadows the worktree-local changes.
Prepend the worktree root so imports resolve here first.
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

_root = str(Path(__file__).parent)
if _root not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _root)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _default_graphite_noop(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """Auto-mock graphite so tests that don't test graphite don't hit gt/gh.

    Tests in test_orchestrator_graphite.py override these with their own
    ``monkeypatch.setattr`` calls, which take effect after this fixture runs
    and win because the last setattr on the same attribute wins.
    """
    import drain_cycle.graphite as _graphite

    _counter: list[int] = [0]

    def _noop_submit(worktree: Path, *, parent: str, body: str = "") -> _graphite.PrInfo:
        _counter[0] += 1
        return _graphite.PrInfo(url="https://github.com/r/p/pull/stub", number=_counter[0])

    monkeypatch.setattr(_graphite, "submit", _noop_submit)
    monkeypatch.setattr(_graphite, "ensure_review_high_label", lambda worktree: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(_graphite, "add_label", lambda pr_number, label, worktree: None)

def build(
    issue: dict[str, Any],
    worktree: Path,
    *,
    resumed: bool = False,
    stack: bool = False,
) -> str:
    title = issue.get("title", "")
    description = issue.get("description") or ""
    identifier = issue.get("identifier", "")

    resume_segment = _resume_directive(identifier) if resumed else ""
    shape_task_segment = _shape_task_directive(identifier) if is_verify_flow(issue) else ""

    if stack:
        preamble = _stack_preamble(identifier, worktree, resume_segment, shape_task_segment)
        tail = _STACK_TAIL
    else:
        preamble = _normal_preamble(identifier, worktree, resume_segment, shape_task_segment)
        tail = _TAIL

    return (
        f"# {title}\n\n"
        f"{description}\n\n"
        f"{preamble}\n"
        f"{tail}\n"
    )

283	**Restack conflict policy (stop-the-line, not auto-merge).** A branch forked off an older `main` shows "needs restack"; `gt restack` rebases it. A restack that hits a **semantic conflict is a stop-the-line**: abort with `git rebase --abort` (`gt abort` refuses in non-interactive mode — use the `git` form), leave the stack on its pre-restack history, and surface the conflict for a human. Never auto-resolve and `gt restack --continue`. (This is the rule the `graphite-stack-review.md` runbook §4 was reconciled to.)
284	
285	<<<<<<< HEAD
286	## 17. `/shape:task` runs inside the worker session; whole-project shaping stays at design-doc scope
287	
288	The M2 worker pipeline introduces a Task Shaper role — `/shape:task` — that runs before the implementer on verify-flow tickets. The initiative doc deferred the invocation interface to this ADR: whether whole-project shaping (via `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown`) pre-computes per-ticket task lists that workers later read, or `/shape:task` runs inside each worker session on its own ticket.
289	
290	**Decision: `/shape:task` runs inside the worker session, invoked once per ticket before the implementer begins.** The skill takes a Linear issue identifier, fetches the live issue from Linear via MCP, and produces an enriched AC checklist + sizing decision + per-stack task list. The output is fed to the implementer in-session and written to the Linear issue body. The Linear write is the durable artefact — a worker resuming a halted issue (§14) reads the existing output from the issue body rather than re-invoking the skill.
291	
292	**Why the per-ticket, in-worker path.** The alternative (pre-computation) would require the operator to run `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown` before any drain can begin, turning the whole-project skill into a planning gate every drain must pass through. `drain-cycle`'s autonomous-drain promise is a single `drain-cycle` invocation, unattended. Fracturing that into "run planning, then drain" creates ceremony the tool exists to remove. A worker that calls `/shape:task` itself is self-contained: the same invocation path works for a cycle drain, a single-ticket re-run, or a §14 resume — no prior planning artefact required.
293	
294	**Rejected alternative: `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown` pre-computes per-ticket task lists.** The whole-project skill runs once before the drain, writes structured per-ticket task lists somewhere (a design doc, a Linear comment, an issue body block), and workers read those artefacts at session start. The appeal is operator review of decomposition before any code runs. The costs are: (a) a mandatory pre-drain gate that breaks the single-invocation promise; (b) a machine-readable output contract that `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown` must emit and every worker must parse — a shared format across two skills and their update paths; (c) stale-data risk when the issue body changes between planning and execution; (d) the only way to know whether the pre-computed list still applies is to re-derive it, making pre-computation an expensive cache that must be manually invalidated. The two skills stay at distinct scopes: `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown` operates on a whole design doc; `/shape:task` operates on a single Linear issue.
295	
296	**`/shape:task`'s input/output contract, as constrained by this decision.**
297	
298	*Input:* A Linear issue identifier. The skill fetches the current issue body, title, and AC from Linear at invocation time. It does not read any prior planning artefact.
299	
300	*Output:*
301	- **Enriched AC checklist** — AC items made concrete, implicit contracts surfaced, irresolvable gaps flagged (the skill notes gaps and continues; it does not hang waiting for operator input).
302	- **Sizing decision** — `single-stack` (all work on one branch) or `N-stacks` (N specified and justified), based on whether the implementation can reach Done in a single PR stack.
303	- **Per-stack task list** — one ordered task list per stack, intended as direct context for the implementer.
304	
305	*Dual-write:* Output is (a) returned to the calling worker for in-session context and (b) appended to the Linear issue body. The Linear write is authoritative: a resumed worker reads the block from the issue body instead of re-running the skill. The skill must emit the output in a stable, delimited format that a future invocation can detect (to avoid silently double-writing).
306	=======
307	## 17. PR links are recorded in the run-log and posted to Linear by the orchestrator
308	
309	After a spawned session exits and the issue is confirmed Done in Linear, the orchestrator needs to close the loop: the operator and any future session must be able to find the PR without reading source or re-running `gh`. Memory lives in artefacts.
310	
311	**Decision.** After confirming Done (`linear.get_issue` returns `completed` state), the orchestrator calls `_find_pr(target_repo, identifier)` — a thin wrapper around `gh pr list --head <branch> --json url,number,labels,baseRefName --limit 1`. If a PR is found, it:
312	
313	1. Records `pr_url`, `pr_number`, `review_high` (mirrors the GitHub `review:high` label), and `parent_branch` (the PR's base ref) in the run-log entry alongside the existing usage fields.
314	2. Posts a comment on the Linear issue via `linear.add_comment` (GraphQL `commentCreate`) with the PR URL and, when flagged, a `review:high` note.
315	
316	All four run-log fields are additive and default to `null`. `grade.py` reads only `cycle_id`, `final_linear_state`, and `exit_code`, so pre-existing run-logs grade unchanged. The Linear comment posting and PR lookup are both non-fatal: any failure (no `gh` binary, no GitHub remote, no PR found, Linear API error) is logged to stderr and the drain continues. The PR link is informational, never load-bearing for the drain's control flow.
317	
318	**Branch name = issue identifier.** The worktree branch is named after the issue identifier (e.g. `ABA-304`) — that is the head branch the orchestrator passes to `gh pr list --head`. The worker's `gt submit` creates the PR with that head, so the lookup is deterministic once the branch name convention is stable.
319	
320	**Why the orchestrator, not the agent.** The spawned agent knows the PR URL immediately after `gt submit`, but the orchestrator is the only component that can write to the run-log — it owns the `RunLog` object and calls `append_entry`. Passing the URL back through the prompt or an out-of-band file would be a second communication channel between the orchestrator and agent; the existing channel (Linear issue state) is already used for the Done signal. The orchestrator re-querying GitHub after the fact is a single, clean read with no new protocol.
321	
322	**Why `gh` CLI, not the GitHub REST/GraphQL API.** `gh` handles authentication transparently (it reads `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`) and determines the repo from the git remote inside the cwd. Adding a GitHub API key to the configuration surface would be a new operator requirement; `gh` is already a prerequisite for the `gt submit` path (Graphite calls `gh` internally).
323	
324	**Alternatives considered.**
325	
326	- *Agent writes PR URL to a side-car file in the worktree (e.g. `.drain-pr.json`).* The orchestrator would read it after the worker exits. Rejected: it introduces a second contract surface between orchestrator and agent beyond the prompt, and the file must be cleaned up to avoid confusing the next `git add`. The `gh pr list` query is stateless and leaves no artefacts.
327	- *Always post the PR comment unconditionally (even on halt).* Rejected: a halted issue may not have a PR, or the PR may be in an intermediate state. Posting a comment on a halted issue would clutter Linear with links to unfinished or abandoned PRs. The comment fires only on confirmed Done.
328	- *Include `review_high` as an orchestrator flag rather than mirroring the GitHub label.* Rejected: the GitHub label is the authoritative signal (applied by the worker agent, visible in the PR UI, used by reviewers); mirroring it avoids a second place for that decision to live.
329	>>>>>>> 35e7053 (feat: record PR links in run-log and post to Linear on Done)
330

- Move to **In Progress** via `mcp__linear-server__save_issue`.
- If the issue isn't yet in the current cycle and you intend to ship it this cycle, assign it to the current cycle.

**On completion:** Before an issue moves to **Done**, all of these must pass in order:

1. **Review** — Run `/code-review-and-quality` against the working-tree changes.
2. **Fix** — Address any Critical or Required findings. Lower-severity findings are at the agent's discretion (fix or note in the summary comment).
3. **Commit + push** — The path here branches by how the issue is being executed:
   - **Direct mode** (interactive session, not spawned by drain-cycle): commit the reviewed version and push to main. This repo pushes directly to main; PRs only when the owner asks. An issue isn't Done if work only exists locally.
   - **Drain mode** (spawned by the drain-cycle orchestrator in a worktree): commit and submit a PR via `gt submit --stack --no-interactive --publish`. The orchestrator automatically posts the PR link back to the Linear issue after the worker exits and the issue is confirmed Done — the agent does not need to post the PR link itself.
4. **Summary comment** — Post a short comment on the Linear issue via `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_comment` with the review summary (count of findings by severity, plus what was fixed vs deferred). In drain mode the orchestrator appends the PR link as a separate comment; the agent's comment is the review summary only.
5. **Done** — Transition to Done via `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue`.

207-- Posts a comment on the Linear issue with the PR link (and a `review:high` flag if the PR carries that label).

209-This lookup uses the `gh` CLI and the branch name (the issue identifier) to find the PR. def test_stack_mode_chains_same_repo_issues_and_forks_different_repo_off_main(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """In stack mode, same-repo issues chain: issue 2's worktree contains
    issue 1's commit in its history. A different-repo issue still forks
    off main and has no cross-repo commits."""
    repo_a = tmp_path / "repo-a"
    repo_b = tmp_path / "repo-b"
    repo_a.mkdir()
    repo_b.mkdir()
    _init_repo(repo_a)
    _init_repo(repo_b)
    monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(tmp_path))

    # Two issues in repo-a, one in repo-b. sort_order drives execution order.
    first = _issue("ABA-1", repo_name="alpha", sort_order=1.0)
    second = _issue("ABA-2", repo_name="alpha", sort_order=2.0)
    other = _issue("ABA-3", repo_name="beta", sort_order=3.0)
    raw_issues = [first, second, other]
    issues_by_id = {i["id"]: i for i in raw_issues}
    marker = tmp_path / "done.txt"

    def fake_pending_issues(cycle_id: str):
        completed = {line for line in _lines(marker)}
        return linear._plan(
            [i for i in raw_issues if i["identifier"] not in completed]
        )

    def fake_get_issue(issue_id: str) -> dict:
        identifier = issues_by_id[issue_id]["identifier"]
        completed = {line for line in _lines(marker)}
        if identifier in completed:
            return {
                **issues_by_id[issue_id],
                "state": {"type": "completed", "name": "Done"},
            }
        return issues_by_id[issue_id]

    monkeypatch.setattr(linear, "current_cycle_id", lambda: "cycle-id")
    monkeypatch.setattr(linear, "pending_issues", fake_pending_issues)
    monkeypatch.setattr(linear, "get_issue", fake_get_issue)
    monkeypatch.setattr(linear, "set_state", lambda issue_id, name: None)

    fake_claude = _write_committing_claude(tmp_path, marker)
    monkeypatch.setattr(orchestrator, "_CLAUDE_CMD", [str(fake_claude)])

    exit_code = orchestrator.run(
        repos.Repos(mapping={"alpha": repo_a, "beta": repo_b}),
        stack=True,
    )
    assert exit_code == 0

    # Worktrees are preserved in stack mode.
    wt_1 = repo_a / ".worktrees" / "ABA-1"
    wt_2 = repo_a / ".worktrees" / "ABA-2"
    wt_3 = repo_b / ".worktrees" / "ABA-3"
    assert wt_1.is_dir()
    assert wt_2.is_dir()
    assert wt_3.is_dir()

    hashes_1 = _git_log_hashes(wt_1)
    hashes_2 = _git_log_hashes(wt_2)
    hashes_3 = _git_log_hashes(wt_3)

    # ABA-1's tip commit appears in ABA-2's history (chain).
    assert hashes_1[0] in hashes_2

    # ABA-3 (different repo) does not contain ABA-1's commit.
    assert hashes_1[0] not in hashes_3

def _lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    return [line for line in path.read_text().splitlines() if line]


def _write_committing_claude(tmp_path: Path, marker: Path) -> Path:
    """Fake ``claude -p`` that makes a git commit in its worktree and records
    its identifier so ``fake_get_issue`` can mark it Done."""
    script = tmp_path / "fake-claude-commit.sh"
    script.write_text(
        "#!/bin/sh\n"
        'id="$(basename "$PWD")"\n'
        'git config user.email "test@example.com"\n'
        'git config user.name "Test"\n'
        'echo "work" > work.txt\n'
        "git add work.txt\n"
        'git commit -m "work for $id"\n'
        f'printf "%s\\n" "$id" >> "{marker}"\n'
    )
    script.chmod(0o755)
    return script


def _git_log_hashes(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Return commit hashes reachable from HEAD in ``path``."""
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "log", "--format=%H"],
        cwd=path,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    return result.stdout.strip().splitlines()

    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """When _find_pr returns a PR, the run-log entry carries the PR fields
    and a Linear comment is posted with the PR link."""
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    repo.mkdir()
    _init_repo(repo)
    monkeypatch.chdir(repo)
    monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", str(tmp_path))

    only = _issue("ABA-ONE", sort_order=1.0)
    raw_issues = [only]
    issues_by_id = {i["id"]: i for i in raw_issues}
    done_marker = tmp_path / "done-identifiers.txt"

    def fake_pending_issues(cycle_id: str):
        completed = _completed_identifiers(done_marker)
        return linear._plan(
            [i for i in raw_issues if i["identifier"] not in completed]
        )

    def fake_get_issue(issue_id: str) -> dict:
        issue = issues_by_id[issue_id]
        if issue["identifier"] in _completed_identifiers(done_marker):
            return {**issue, "state": {"type": "completed", "name": "Done"}}
        return issue

    monkeypatch.setattr(linear, "current_cycle_id", lambda: "stub-cycle-id")
    monkeypatch.setattr(linear, "pending_issues", fake_pending_issues)
    monkeypatch.setattr(linear, "get_issue", fake_get_issue)
    monkeypatch.setattr(linear, "set_state", lambda issue_id, state_name: None)

    # Stub _find_pr to return a fake PR.
    fake_pr = {
        "pr_url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/7",
        "pr_number": 7,
        "review_high": True,
        "parent_branch": "main",
    }
    monkeypatch.setattr(orchestrator, "_find_pr", lambda repo, branch: fake_pr)

    # Capture add_comment calls.
    posted_comments: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        linear, "add_comment",
        lambda issue_id, body: posted_comments.append((issue_id, body)),
    )

    fake_claude = _write_fake_claude_script(tmp_path, done_marker)
    monkeypatch.setattr(orchestrator, "_CLAUDE_CMD", [str(fake_claude)])

    exit_code = orchestrator.run(repos.Repos(mapping={"test-repo": repo}))
    assert exit_code == 0

    # PR fields are in the run-log entry.
    runs_dir = tmp_path / ".drain-cycle" / "runs"
    payload = json.loads(next(runs_dir.glob("stub-cycle-id-*.json")).read_text())
    (entry,) = payload["entries"]
    assert entry["pr_url"] == "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/7"
    assert entry["pr_number"] == 7
    assert entry["review_high"] is True
    assert entry["parent_branch"] == "main"

    # A Linear comment was posted with the PR link.
    assert len(posted_comments) == 1
    issue_id, body = posted_comments[0]
    assert issue_id == "id-ABA-ONE"
    assert "https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/7" in body
    assert "review:high" in body


def _completed_identifiers(marker: Path) -> set[str]:
    if not marker.exists():
        return set()
    return {line for line in marker.read_text().splitlines() if line}


def _write_fake_claude_script(tmp_path: Path, done_marker: Path) -> Path:
    script = tmp_path / "fake-claude.sh"
    script.write_text(
        "#!/bin/sh\n"
        f'printf "%s\\n" "$(basename "$PWD")" >> "{done_marker}"\n'
    )
    script.chmod(0o755)
    return script


def _write_streaming_claude_script(tmp_path: Path, done_marker: Path) -> Path:
    """A ``claude -p`` stand-in that marks the issue Done *and* emits a
    canned stream-json sequence (two turns + a result) to stdout, so the
    worker has real usage to parse."""
    stream_lines = [
        json.dumps({"type": "system", "subtype": "init", "session_id": "sess-1"}),
        json.dumps(
            {
                "type": "assistant",
                "message": {
                    "id": "msg_a",
                    "usage": {
                        "input_tokens": 10,
                        "output_tokens": 4,
                        "cache_creation_input_tokens": 100,
                        "cache_read_input_tokens": 0,
                    },
                },
            }

All evidence gathered. Sanity check: I re-ran the full suite myself (289 passed), read every control-flow branch in orchestrator.py directly, diffed all three source branches against their fork point and traced each functional element into `integrate-stacking`, and checked every claim in the request against fresh tool output rather than the integration notes.

## Verdict

**Not ready to push as claimed — one of your eight claims (check 8) is factually false in the code, plus two stale-doc leftovers.** Everything else verified: nothing functional vanished, the control flow is correct, tests are green. The fixes are small (one validation loop + two doc paragraphs); after them this is push-ready.

## Findings, by severity

**1. MEDIUM — `push_to_main_repos` membership validation does not exist.** Your claim 8 says parsing "validates type and membership against the repos mapping." It validates type only. `_parse_push_to_main_repos` (`/Users/anton/src/drain-cycle/drain_cycle/repos.py:132-153`) checks list-ness and non-empty strings; `load()` (lines 197-204) never compares entries against `mapping`. The docstring at lines 135-136 even promises "must be a list of repo names matching entries in the `repos:` block" — promise unimplemented (inherited verbatim from ABA-303, which had the same gap). Consequence: a typo'd repo name is silently accepted and that repo **stacks** when the operator opted it out — the exact misconfiguration the option exists to prevent. No test covers membership either (`tests/test_repos.py:316-390` cover only absent-key/non-list/non-string/empty-string).

**2. MEDIUM-LOW — zero test coverage of `--no-stack` actually being parsed as True.** `grep -rn '\-\-no-stack' tests/` returns nothing; `tests/test_cli.py` only asserts `no_stack: False` (lines 116, 285). Commit 4ef7761 claims test alignment with the stacking default, but the opt-out flag's positive path is verified only by my reading of `cli.py:60,77,92`.

**3. LOW — `runlog.py` docstring carries ABA-304's dropped design.** `/Users/anton/src/drain-cycle/drain_cycle/runlog.py:83-90`: "no GitHub PR was found (pre-PR workflow, halted issues, or `gh` unavailable)" — under the integrated design `gh` failure is a stop-the-line halt, never a silent null — and "the `review:high` GitHub label **the worker applies**" — the orchestrator applies it (orchestrator.py:753-757). This is exactly the "leftover claim that the worker does GitHub work" your check 6 hunts for, just in a module docstring rather than the three named docs.

**4. LOW — README walkthrough is stale under stack-as-default.** `/Users/anton/src/drain-cycle/README.md:140-143`: the example transcript narrates "(… claude -p session … commits, **pushes**, marks the issue Done …)" and "ABA-241 done; worktree removed." — that's now the opt-out path; the default-mode worker doesn't push and the success line is "done; PR <url>." (orchestrator.py:850-856). Pre-existing text the integration didn't touch, but ABA-303's default flip made it wrong.

**5. OBSERVATION — stack continuity is per-invocation only.** `last_branch_per_repo` is an in-memory dict (orchestrator.py:347). After any halt + re-run — including `add_label` failing *after* a successful submit (line 755, inside the try, before the line-758 update) — the Done issue is skipped on re-run and the next issue parents onto `main`, not the already-submitted PR branch. Inherited from ABA-302's design, not an integration regression, but undocumented in §16/§18.

**6. OBSERVATION — cli flag asymmetry.** `drain-cycle grade --no-stack` silently runs grade with the flag ignored, while `grade --watch` exits 2 (cli.py:94-104 guard on `not watch` only). Pre-existing pattern extended.

**7. PRE-EXISTING — 4 ruff F-lints, all in test files untouched or unmodified-at-that-line by the integration** (`tests/test_orchestrator_marker.py:10,16` F401, `tests/test_orchestrator_halt.py:693` F841 — present on main at line 689, `tests/test_orchestrator_teardown.py:69` F841). Not yours.

## What verified clean (with evidence)

1. **Tests/status:** `uv run pytest -q` → **289 passed, 0 failed** (28.8s). Branch `integrate-stacking`, no modified tracked files; one unrelated untracked file `docs/initiative-multi-agent-collaboration.html` won't be swept into a push.
2. **Conflict markers:** `git grep` for all three marker forms → zero hits.
3. **Functional completeness:** diffed all three branches against fork point 093c83d. ABA-302: graphite.py (now with title kwarg), assembly block, conftest auto-mock — all present; its handoff variant is the stated delta. ABA-303: cli flags, no_stack threading, repos parsing, repos.example.yml block — all present; its prompt rewrite is the stated delta (main's `_stack_preamble` kept, `stack=False` default at prompt.py:132, orchestrator passes it explicitly at line 552). ABA-304: `linear.add_comment` (linear.py:309), four run-log fields (runlog.py:186-189, 217-220), Linear comment block (orchestrator.py:786-798) — all present; `_find_pr` is the stated delta, zero references remain. **Nothing silently vanished.**
4. **Control flow:** `stack` computed per-issue at orchestrator.py:505 from both opt-outs, *before* base selection at 506-510; graphite failure returns at line 784 before teardown (800-803), worktree preserved; success path tears down; `last_branch_per_repo` updates only at 758 inside the try; Linear comment is try/except-wrapped and uses `submitted_pr`; Done entry (812-830) carries flow + both verdicts + all four PR fields. Branch chaining works because `worktree.remove` uses `git worktree remove --force` without deleting the branch (worktree.py:155-160), and `test_graphite_submit_receives_main_then_first_branch` proves main→first-branch parenting end-to-end against a real git repo.
5. **Imports:** all nine modules import; ruff F401/F811/F821/F841 clean across `drain_cycle/`.
6. **Docs:** AGENTS.md:29, README "PR links" (204-209), design-decisions §16/§17/§18 all consistently orchestrator-assembles; §17 collision resolved; §18 explicitly rejects the post-hoc lookup. Only the two leftovers above (findings 3, 4).
7. **cli.py:** `--no-stack` parsed (lines 60, 77), passed as `no_stack` (92), in usage (47, 56), unknown args exit 2 (108-110) with test coverage for the exit-2 path.
8. **repos.py:** type validation and absent-key→`()` confirmed; membership validation absent (finding 1).

def _parse_push_to_main_repos(value: Any) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Validate the optional ``push_to_main_repos`` key.

    ``None`` (key absent) yields the default (empty tuple). A present value
    must be a list of repo names matching entries in the ``repos:`` block.
    Every failure raises ``RepoConfigError`` naming the offending entry.
    """
    if value is None:
        return ()
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        raise RepoConfigError(
            f"{_CONFIG_DISPLAY} 'push_to_main_repos' must be a list"
        )
    entries: list[str] = []
    for entry in value:
        if not isinstance(entry, str) or not entry.strip():
            raise RepoConfigError(
                f"{_CONFIG_DISPLAY} 'push_to_main_repos' entry {entry!r}: "
                "must be a non-empty string"
            )
        entries.append(entry)
    return tuple(entries)


def load(path: Path | None = None) -> Repos:
    """Read ``repos.yml`` and return a validated ``Repos``.

    Tilde-prefixed paths inside the file are expanded against ``$HOME``.
    Every failure mode raises ``RepoConfigError`` with a message that
            raise RepoConfigError(

    worktree_config_paths = _parse_worktree_config_paths(

        worktree_config_paths=worktree_config_paths,
